What walked past while they ate?

stories.text: On Tuesday, Chiamaka took the early train from Varrow to visit her grandmother. She left her umbrella on the train, and a conductor named Mr Ilves put it in the lost property office at Ashgrove station. Chiamaka spent the afternoon with her grandmother baking bread. That evening she collected the umbrella from Ashgrove on her way home.
qs: Where did Chiamaka leave her umbrella?
Who put the umbrella in the lost property office?
Where was the umbrella in the afternoon?
What did Chiamaka do in the afternoon?

stories.text: A delivery van blocked Orchard Road for two hours on Thursday after its back wheel came off. The driver, Mr Wisniewski, was not hurt. A mechanic from the garage on Fell Street fitted a new wheel, while a police officer named Constable Ntuli directed the traffic. The road was open again before the school buses came.
qs: Who was the driver of the van?
How long was the road blocked?

stories.text: A lazy cat named Dumpling slept on the warm roof of a bakery. Every morning a sparrow woke him by singing on the chimney. One day Dumpling chased the sparrow away so he could sleep longer. The next morning no one woke him, and he slept through the moment when the baker threw out the broken pastries. A pigeon ate them all, and Dumpling went hungry until night.
qs: What did Dumpling do to the sparrow?
What did the baker throw out?

stories.text: The lighthouse keeper, Mr Thorvaldsen, kept a spare lantern in the boathouse. On Sunday morning his son Edvin rowed the lantern across to the island because the old lamp had cracked. By lunchtime the new lantern hung at the top of the lighthouse. Edvin rowed back in the evening with the cracked lamp in the bottom of the boat.
qs: Where was the spare lantern kept?
Who rowed the lantern across to the island?
Where was the new lantern by lunchtime?
What was in the bottom of the boat in the evening?
When did Edvin row the lantern across?

stories.text: Grandpa Sotiris promised to teach his granddaughter, Leni, how to fish. They waited on the jetty all morning and caught nothing. Leni grew bored and began to sketch the boats, and that was when her line tugged hard. She pulled in a silver mackerel, which Grandpa Sotiris cooked for supper.
qs: Who promised to teach Leni to fish?
Where did they wait all morning?
What did Leni begin to sketch?
What did Grandpa Sotiris do with the mackerel?

stories.text: A beaver named Brannoc built his dam faster than any beaver in the forest, but he never helped the others. When a flood broke his dam, he asked his neighbours to help him fix it. The old heron, who had watched him for years, told the beavers to help anyway. They rebuilt the dam in one night, and Brannoc spent the next summer mending everyone else's lodges.
qs: Who told the beavers to help anyway?
How long did it take to rebuild the dam?
What did Brannoc do the next summer?

stories.text: Before school, Laleh put her library book in her bag. At break she lent it to her friend Shinpei, who read it under the oak tree in the playground. After lunch Shinpei left it on his desk, and the teacher, Mrs Sjoberg, put it on the shelf by the window. Laleh found it there at home time.
qs: Where was the book before school?
Who had the book at break?
Where did Shinpei read the book?
Who put the book on the shelf?
Where was the book at home time?

stories.text: The beekeeper, Mr Tavares, wore a white suit and a net over his face. On Saturday his neighbour's dog knocked over one of the hives in the yard. Mr Tavares calmed the bees with smoke and lifted the hive back onto its stand. The neighbour, Mrs Quinlan, brought him a lemon cake to say sorry.
qs: What knocked over one of the hives?
How did Mr Tavares calm the bees?
What did Mrs Quinlan bring him?
When did the dog knock over the hive?

stories.text: A crab and a gull lived on the same rock. The gull, Merel, liked to boast about flying, and the crab, Ludo, liked to boast about his shell. One afternoon a storm blew Merel into a crack in the rock where she could not open her wings. Ludo crawled into the crack and pushed her out with his claws. After that, the gull never laughed at the crab's slow walk.
qs: Who liked to boast about flying?
What did Ludo like to boast about?
What blew Merel into a crack?
Where did the storm blow Merel?
What did Ludo push her out with?

stories.text: Mr Obiora drove his van of pumpkins from the farm to the town square on Saturday morning. Halfway there he stopped at a petrol station, where a boy named Teo bought two pumpkins. In the square Mr Obiora sold the rest by noon. He drove home through the hills and reached the farm just after dark.
qs: What was in Mr Obiora's van?
Where did Mr Obiora stop halfway?
When had Mr Obiora sold the rest?
When did he reach the farm?

stories.text: Dr Nwosu, the village vet, was called to a farm at midnight because a cow was having a calf. The farmer, Bertil, held a torch while she worked. The calf was born just before one o'clock, and Bertil's children named it Pepper. In the morning Dr Nwosu had breakfast at the farmhouse before she drove back to her clinic.
qs: What did Bertil's children name the calf?
Where did Dr Nwosu have breakfast?

stories.text: A young owl named Hollis could not stay awake at night like the other owls. She asked a bat what to do, and the bat told her to sleep through the bright afternoon. Hollis tried it, but the noisy squirrels in her tree kept waking her. In the end a badger let her sleep in his quiet burrow, and she hunted all night with her brothers.
qs: Who could not stay awake at night?
Who told Hollis to sleep through the afternoon?
Who let Hollis sleep in his burrow?
What did Hollis do all night?

stories.text: At eight the caretaker, Mr Delacroix, unlocked the museum and hung the key on a hook in the office. At ten a guide named Devika took the key to open the map room. She forgot to return it and carried it in her pocket all day. When the museum closed, Mr Delacroix found the key in Devika's coat, which was hanging in the staff room.
qs: Where was the key at nine?
Who took the key at ten?
Why did Devika take the key?
Where was the key when the museum closed?

stories.text: Firefighters rescued a kitten from the roof of the Moravec bakery on Tuesday. The kitten, which belongs to the baker's son, Matyas, had climbed up a drainpipe. A ladder was raised by the crew, and firefighter Leah Strand carried the kitten down in a basket. Matyas gave the crew a tray of cinnamon buns.
qs: What did Matyas give the crew?
Where was the kitten rescued from?

stories.text: A squirrel named Nutmeg hid acorns in twenty places around the pond, but she forgot where most of them were. A jay, who had watched her, offered to tell her the places in return for half the acorns. Nutmeg agreed, and they dug up eighteen acorns together. In spring the two acorns they missed grew into small oak trees.
qs: Who hid acorns around the pond?
How many places did Nutmeg hide acorns in?
Who offered to tell Nutmeg the places?
What did the jay want in return?
What did the missed acorns grow into?

stories.text: Lars and his sister Bozena took the morning ferry to Tarnholm Island with a picnic basket. They left the basket in the shade of a pine tree while they swam. A goat wandered over and ate their sandwiches. In the afternoon they bought fish soup at a cafe by the pier, and they caught the last ferry home at six.
qs: Where did they leave the picnic basket?
Where did they buy fish soup?
When did they catch the last ferry home?

stories.text: Mrs Quaresma, the school librarian, ordered forty new books in September. They arrived in two boxes, but one box was sent to the wrong school by mistake. A driver named Fiifi brought the missing box back a week later. The pupils helped Mrs Quaresma put stickers on every book before the reading fair.
qs: How many new books did Mrs Quaresma order?
Who brought the missing box back?
Where was one box sent by mistake?
What did the pupils put on every book?

stories.text: A peacock named Amadou spent every morning admiring his tail in the pond. A plain brown hen, Clementine, spent her mornings scratching for worms. When winter came, the peacock had nothing stored, but the hen had a pile of dry seeds under the barn. Clementine shared the seeds, and Amadou kept her warm under his wide tail on the coldest nights.
qs: Who admired his tail in the pond?
Where did the hen keep her seeds?
What did Amadou do on the coldest nights?

stories.text: Seung-woo cycled from his flat to the bakery at seven to buy rolls. He locked his bicycle to a lamppost outside, but when he came out a tyre was flat. He wheeled the bicycle to Mr Petrakis's repair shop on the corner. While the tyre was being fixed, Seung-woo ate two rolls on the bench outside, and he rode home at half past eight.
qs: Where did Seung-woo cycle at seven?
Where did Seung-woo lock his bicycle?
Whose repair shop did Seung-woo take the bicycle to?
Where did Seung-woo eat two rolls?

stories.text: In the tax office on the third floor, a clerk named Zubair kept a fern on his windowsill. When he went on holiday, his colleague Marguerite watered it every Monday. The fern grew so big that the manager, Mr Aaltonen, asked to move it to the meeting room. Zubair came back and found his fern at the end of the long table.
qs: What did Zubair keep on his windowsill?
Who asked to move the fern?
Where was the fern when Zubair came back?
When did Marguerite water the fern?

stories.text: Two ants, Kip and Marlo, found a strawberry too heavy to carry. Kip wanted to call the whole nest, but Marlo wanted to keep it secret. While they argued, a beetle rolled the strawberry down the hill. Marlo ran home to fetch help, and twenty ants carried it back up before sunset.
qs: Who wanted to call the whole nest?
Who wanted to keep the strawberry secret?
What rolled the strawberry down the hill?
How many ants carried the strawberry back up?
When did the ants carry the strawberry back up?

stories.text: A tour bus left the Brightwater Hotel at nine with a guide named Mrs Ocampo. The group spent the morning at the salt mine and had lunch in a village called Rennick. One tourist, Mr Haugen, left his camera at the restaurant. The driver went back for it while the others visited the cathedral, and the bus returned to the hotel at five.
qs: Where did the group spend the morning?
What did Mr Haugen leave at the restaurant?
Who went back for the camera?
What did the others do while the driver went back?

stories.text: The cook at the Heron Inn, Rocio, burned the soup on a busy Saturday. Her assistant, a tall boy called Ikenna, ran to the market for more onions. While he was gone, Rocio made a bean stew instead, and the guests liked it so much that it went on the menu.
qs: What did Ikenna go to the market for?

stories.text: A mole named Grig dug a tunnel under the garden fence to reach the carrots. The rabbit, who owned the carrot patch, was angry at first. Then Grig showed her that the tunnel led straight to the stream, where the water was clean. The rabbit let him eat one carrot a day, and she used his tunnel to fetch water.
qs: Who dug a tunnel under the garden fence?
How many carrots could Grig eat a day?
What did the rabbit use the tunnel for?

stories.text: A parcel for Mrs Villalobos was left on the wrong doorstep on Monday. Her neighbour, Ibrahim, took it inside to keep it dry. On Tuesday Ibrahim's daughter carried the parcel across the street to Mrs Villalobos's porch. Mrs Villalobos opened it that evening and found the wool she had ordered.
qs: Who carried the parcel across the street?
Where was the parcel on Tuesday evening?

stories.text: Every spring the gardeners of Brackenfield Allotments hold a contest for the longest bean. This year a retired pilot, Mr Brennan, won with a bean as long as his arm. The judge, Mrs Kaur, measured it twice to be sure. His prize was a new watering can, which he gave to the youngest gardener, a girl named Ragnhild.
qs: How many times did Mrs Kaur measure the bean?
Who did Mr Brennan give the prize to?

stories.text: A fox cub called Rasko found a shiny bottle cap and thought it was a gold coin. He hid it under a stone and guarded it for three days without hunting. A weasel told him the cap was worthless, so Rasko, who was very hungry by then, went back to hunting. The next morning a crow stole the cap, but Rasko only laughed.
qs: What did Rasko think the cap was?
Where did Rasko hide the cap?
Who told Rasko the cap was worthless?

stories.text: On the school trip, Mr Abiodun carried the first-aid kit in his rucksack. At the waterfall he gave it to a parent, Mrs Yamada, because he had to go back for a lost glove. Mrs Yamada used a plaster from the kit when a boy named Sorin cut his knee on a rock. By the time the group reached the car park, the kit was back in Mr Abiodun's rucksack.
qs: Who had the first-aid kit after Mr Abiodun gave it away?
Why did Mr Abiodun go back?
What did Mrs Yamada use from the kit?
Where was the kit when the group reached the car park?

stories.text: The violinist, Wiebke, left her violin backstage at the concert hall after the rehearsal on Friday. A stagehand named Bogdan locked it in the instrument cupboard for the night. On Saturday morning Wiebke could not find it and was very worried. Bogdan arrived at ten with the key, and the concert began on time that evening.
qs: When did Wiebke leave her violin backstage?
Where did Wiebke leave her violin?
Who locked the violin in the cupboard?
Where was the violin on Friday night?
When did Bogdan arrive with the key?

stories.text: Every morning the lock-keeper, Gesine Brandt, opened the upper gates before the first barge arrived. On Tuesday a barge called the Kittiwake carried coal down from the quarry, and its skipper, Ruairi, waved a newspaper at her. Gesine made tea in her cottage while the water slowly dropped. When the lower gates were finally opened, Ruairi left the newspaper on her bench and steered the barge toward the town.
qs: Who was the skipper of the Kittiwake?
What did Ruairi wave at Gesine?
Where did Ruairi leave the newspaper?

stories.text: A hedgehog named Tibbet kept a store of beechnuts under a fallen log. One windy evening a magpie flew down and asked to borrow a single nut for her chicks. Tibbet refused, because he was afraid the magpie would come back for more. That night a gust of wind blew the log away, and the beechnuts rolled into the stream. In the morning the magpie brought him a worm, and the hedgehog felt ashamed.
qs: Who kept a store of beechnuts?
Where did Tibbet keep his beechnuts?
Who asked to borrow a nut?
What did the magpie bring Tibbet in the morning?

stories.text: At dawn the caravan left the well at Qasr Tamim with forty camels. The guide, Yahya, rode at the front with the water skins, and his niece Samira counted the camels each hour. By noon they had reached a line of red dunes, where they rested in the shade of a rock. In the evening the caravan came to the market town of Ain Selmat, and Samira sold the salt there.
qs: How many camels did the caravan have?
Where was the caravan at noon?
When did the caravan reach Ain Selmat?

stories.text: The post office in Kellerby opens at eight, but on Friday the clerk, Mr Vandersloot, was late because his bicycle had a flat tyre. A queue of six people waited outside in the rain. The first in line was Mrs Nwachukwu, who needed to send a parcel of knitted scarves to her grandson. When Mr Vandersloot finally unlocked the door, he gave everyone a stamp for free.
qs: Who was the clerk at the post office?
Who was first in the queue?
What did Mrs Nwachukwu want to send?

stories.text: Two crows, Ashby and Pella, found a shiny spoon on a picnic blanket. Ashby wanted to hide it in the church tower, but Pella wanted to give it to the old owl who lived in the elm. While they argued, a squirrel ran off with the spoon. The squirrel dropped it into the duck pond, and neither crow ever saw it again.
qs: What did the two crows find?
Where did Ashby want to hide the spoon?
What ran off with the spoon?
Where did the spoon end up?

stories.text: Liesbeth arrived at the ski lodge on Monday afternoon and left her skis in the drying room. On Tuesday morning she took the chairlift to the top station, where her brother Matthias was waiting with a thermos. They skied down together to the lower village for lunch. In the evening Matthias carried both pairs of skis back to the lodge, but Liesbeth stayed in the village to watch a film.
qs: Where did Liesbeth leave her skis on Monday?
Who was waiting at the top station?
When did Matthias carry the skis back to the lodge?
Where were Liesbeth's skis on Tuesday evening?
What did Liesbeth stay in the village to do?

stories.text: At the printing works on Saddler Lane, the foreman, Ferenc, checked every poster before it was sent out. On Wednesday a young apprentice named Rukhsana spotted a mistake in the date of the harvest fair. Ferenc stopped the press, and the wrong posters were cut up for scrap paper. The corrected posters were printed after lunch and delivered to the town hall by van.
qs: What did Ferenc do when the mistake was found?
Where were the corrected posters delivered?
When were the corrected posters printed?

stories.text: A young goat named Brisk wanted to cross the river to taste the clover on the far bank. The heron told him to wait for the dry season, but Brisk did not listen. He jumped onto a floating branch, which carried him downstream to the mill. The miller's dog pulled him out of the water, and Brisk walked home slowly, cold and wet.
qs: Who wanted to cross the river?
What did Brisk want to taste?
Who told Brisk to wait for the dry season?
Who pulled Brisk out of the water?

stories.text: Before sunrise the fishing boat Gaviota left the harbour at Puerto Leiva with three crew. The captain, Jacinta, steered toward the rocks beyond the lighthouse, where the mackerel were running. By mid-morning the nets were full and the boat turned back. The catch was unloaded at the fish market, and the crew ate breakfast at a stall on the quay.
qs: Who was the captain of the Gaviota?
How many crew were on the boat?
What was running near the rocks?

stories.text: The choir met in the chapel hall every Thursday at seven. This week the conductor, Ms Sandvik, had a cold, so the pianist, Arturo, led the rehearsal instead. The tenors kept singing too fast, and Arturo tapped his pencil on the piano to slow them down. At the end, a soprano named Wairimu handed out copies of the new carol.
qs: Who led the rehearsal this week?
Why did Arturo lead the rehearsal?
What did Arturo tap on the piano?
Who handed out copies of the new carol?

stories.text: A fox named Rusk and a badger named Moss shared a den under a hawthorn hedge. Every night Rusk brought back eggs, and Moss swept the den with his tail. One night the farmer's lantern frightened Rusk, and he came home with nothing. Moss gave him half of his own supper of beetles, and the fox never forgot it.
qs: Where did Rusk and Moss live?
What did Rusk bring back every night?
What did Moss give the fox?

stories.text: At nine o'clock the gardener, Fenwick, wheeled a tray of orchids from the potting shed to the glasshouse. Later that morning a visitor, Dr Ilunga, asked to see the giant water lily, so Fenwick led her to the lily pond. After lunch the orchids were moved again, this time to the shop by the main gate. By closing time three of them had been sold.
qs: Who wheeled the tray of orchids?
Where were the orchids taken at nine o'clock?
Who asked to see the giant water lily?
Where were the orchids after lunch?
How many orchids had been sold by closing time?

stories.text: Ebo lives above a bakery on Tannery Row, and his neighbour, Mrs Dunleavy, lives on the ground floor. On Saturday her cat climbed onto the roof and would not come down. Ebo fetched a ladder from the bakery and carried the cat back to her in a laundry basket. To thank him, Mrs Dunleavy baked him a lemon cake.
qs: Who lives on the ground floor?
Where did Ebo get the ladder?
What did Ebo carry the cat in?
What did Mrs Dunleavy bake for Ebo?

stories.text: A mole named Grummel was proud of his long tunnels and laughed at the robin, who could only hop. When a spring flood filled the meadow, Grummel's tunnels were the first to go under water. The robin flew to the top of the gatepost and called the other animals to the high ground. Grummel followed her voice and was saved.
qs: Who was proud of his tunnels?

stories.text: On the first day of the trip, Leocadia and her father took the night train from Varnholm to the coast. They slept in a narrow cabin and woke up at Sennby, where the sea was grey and calm. In the afternoon they rode a ferry to a small island and hired bicycles from a farmer. The next morning Leocadia left her red scarf on the ferry, and her father had to go back for it.
qs: Where did they go in the afternoon?
Who did they hire bicycles from?
Where did Leocadia leave her red scarf?

stories.text: The vet, Dr Sithole, had a busy Monday. In the morning she treated a sheepdog that had cut its paw on a broken bottle. At noon a boy called Bartosz brought in a rabbit that would not eat, and she found a seed stuck in its teeth. Her assistant, Lorna, answered the telephone all afternoon while Dr Sithole drove out to a farm to see a sick cow.
qs: What had the sheepdog cut its paw on?
What was stuck in the rabbit's teeth?
Who answered the telephone all afternoon?

stories.text: A peacock named Sultan told the hens that his feathers made him king of the yard. The hens chose a quiet old goose instead, because she always warned them when the fox was near. Sultan sulked behind the cart shed for a whole day. In the end he learned to keep watch from the barn roof, and the goose let him help.
qs: Who said he was king of the yard?
Who did the hens choose instead?
Why did the hens choose the goose?
What did Sultan do behind the cart shed?

stories.text: At seven the baker's van left the depot with sixty loaves. Its driver, Gaspard, stopped first at the school, where he left twenty loaves in the kitchen. Next he drove to the hospital and unloaded thirty more. The last ten loaves went to a café by the river, and by half past nine the van was empty and back at the depot.
qs: How many loaves did Gaspard leave at the school?
When did the baker's van leave the depot?
Where was the van at half past nine?

stories.text: Grandma Philippa keeps her button tin on the top shelf of the sewing cupboard. On Sunday her grandson Chibuzo needed a button for his school coat. He stood on a stool to reach the tin, but the stool wobbled and the tin fell, spilling buttons across the kitchen floor. Philippa laughed and helped him pick them up, and they found a brass button that matched.
qs: Where does Philippa keep her button tin?
Who needed a button for his coat?
What spilled across the kitchen floor?

stories.text: A spider named Wennick spun her web across the door of the potting shed. Every morning the gardener's broom tore it down, and every night she spun it again. A wren watched her and asked why she did not move. Wennick said that the shed door caught the most moths. The next spring the gardener left the door open, and the web stayed whole all summer.
qs: Who spun a web across the door?
What tore the web down every morning?
Who asked the spider why she did not move?
Why did Wennick keep her web on the shed door?
What did the gardener do the next spring?

stories.text: On Monday the museum's old globe was carried from the library to the restorer's workshop in the basement. The restorer, Torleif, cleaned it for three days and painted over a crack near the equator. On Thursday a porter named Delphine took the globe upstairs to the map room. It stood there for the opening of the exhibition on Saturday.
qs: Where was the globe on Tuesday?
Where was the globe on Saturday?

stories.text: Before work, Priyanka dropped her shoes at the cobbler's and her coat at the dry cleaner's. At lunchtime she collected a prescription from the chemist on Pellow Street. On her way home she picked up the coat, but the cobbler had closed early, so the shoes stayed there until morning.
qs: What did Priyanka collect at lunchtime?
Where did she collect the prescription?
What did Priyanka drop at the cobbler's?
Where were the shoes that night?
When did she collect the prescription?

stories.text: A pair of otters, Tassie and Brann, were building a slide down the riverbank. Tassie carried smooth stones while Brann packed the mud. A kingfisher told them the slide would never work, but the otters kept going. By evening the slide was finished, and even the kingfisher tried it once.
qs: Who said the slide would never work?

stories.text: The mail sack for the island was loaded onto a small plane at Tollerby airfield at eight. The pilot, Captain Ogunleye, flew it across the bay to the grass strip at Haverstrand. There the postmistress, Elin, put it in the back of her tractor and drove it to the village shop. By eleven the letters had been sorted, and the parcel for the lighthouse was still waiting on the counter.
qs: Who flew the mail across the bay?
What did Elin put the sack in?
Where did Elin drive the sack?
Where was the parcel for the lighthouse at eleven?

stories.text: A farmer in the hills above Lorvan found a lost hiker on Tuesday night. The hiker, a student named Solange, had twisted her ankle near the old quarry. The farmer, Arkady Volkov, heard her whistle and carried her to his farmhouse on his back. She was taken to hospital the next morning by ambulance.
qs: Where had Solange twisted her ankle?
How was Solange taken to hospital?

stories.text: A raven named Sable guarded the orchard for the farmer in return for the windfall apples. One autumn a band of jays offered him the whole crop if he would look the other way. Sable pretended to agree, then flew to the farmhouse and cawed until the farmer came out. The jays fled, and the farmer left a basket of apples on the wall for the raven.
qs: What did the raven get in return for guarding?
Who offered the raven the whole crop?
Where did the farmer leave a basket of apples?

stories.text: Mirela and Joaquín set out from the hut at the foot of the pass at six. They climbed to the saddle by nine, where they ate bread and cheese beside a cairn. A storm came over the ridge in the afternoon, so they turned back and reached the hut again before dark. Joaquín's camera was left at the cairn and was found by another climber a week later.
qs: When did they reach the saddle?
What did they eat beside the cairn?
Whose camera was left at the cairn?

stories.text: The school caretaker, Mr Fairbairn, unlocks the gates at half past seven every morning. On Wednesday he found a goose sitting on the steps of the gym. The headteacher, Ms Arriaga, telephoned the park ranger, who arrived with a large blanket. The goose was carried back to the park lake, and lessons started only ten minutes late.
qs: What did Mr Fairbairn find on the steps of the gym?
What did the park ranger bring?

stories.text: A young bat named Fennick was afraid of the dark, which made the other bats laugh. One night a moth showed him how the moon lit the edges of the trees. Fennick practised flying along the lane behind the moth until dawn. After that he led the colony to the best feeding grounds by the marsh.
qs: Who was afraid of the dark?
What lit the edges of the trees?
Who did Fennick lead to the feeding grounds?
Where were the best feeding grounds?

stories.text: The crate of oranges was lifted off the ship at Port Ellery on Monday. It spent the night in a warehouse on the east dock, and on Tuesday a lorry took it inland to the market at Dunmarrow. A greengrocer named Seo-yeon bought the whole crate and stacked the oranges in her shop window. By Friday only a dozen were left.
qs: Where was the crate on Monday night?
Where did Seo-yeon stack the oranges?
How many oranges were left by Friday?

stories.text: Anneliese runs a small tailor's shop next to the tram stop. On Thursday a nervous groom, Leopold, brought in a suit with a torn sleeve two hours before his wedding. Anneliese mended the sleeve while Leopold paced up and down, and her son ran to the florist to fetch his buttonhole. Leopold reached the church just in time.
qs: What did Anneliese do while Leopold paced?
Who brought in a suit with a torn sleeve?

stories.text: A beaver named Hobb built a dam that flooded the frogs' reed bed. The frogs complained to the old pike who ruled the river. The pike told Hobb to leave a gap in the dam for the water to pass. Hobb grumbled, but he made the gap, and by summer the reed bed was green again.
qs: Who did the frogs complain to?
What did the pike tell Hobb to leave in the dam?
When was the reed bed green again?

stories.text: A library book about volcanoes was borrowed by a girl named Adwoa on the first of May. She took it on holiday to her aunt's house in the mountains and read it on the balcony. On the way home she left it on a bus, and the driver handed it in at the bus station. Three weeks later a clerk from the station brought it back to the library.
qs: Where did Adwoa read the book?
Who brought the book back to the library?
When did Adwoa borrow the book?

stories.text: Every evening at six, Mrs Anozie closes her newspaper kiosk on the corner of the square. Last Friday a man in a grey hat left his umbrella on the counter. She kept it under the till for a week, and on the next Friday the man came back for it. He was so pleased that he bought every copy of the evening paper she had left.
qs: When does Mrs Anozie close her kiosk?
What did the man leave on the counter?
Where did Mrs Anozie keep the umbrella?
What did the man buy when he came back?

stories.text: A sparrow named Chirrup lived on the same farm as a sleepy cat called Marmalade. The cat promised never to chase her if she would wake him whenever the farmer's wife put out milk. For a whole summer the sparrow kept her side of the bargain. Then one morning Marmalade forgot and pounced, and Chirrup escaped only by flying into the chimney. After that she woke the dog instead.
qs: Who promised never to chase the sparrow?
What did Marmalade do one morning?
Who did Chirrup wake after that?

stories.text: In the morning the site engineer, Rahim, left his blue notebook in the site office. At ten the architect, Ms Kouris, picked it up by mistake and took it to her car. She drove to the council offices for a meeting and only noticed the notebook when she opened her bag. In the afternoon she posted it back to Rahim, who got it on Thursday.
qs: Where did Rahim leave his notebook?
Who had the notebook after ten?
Where did Ms Kouris drive for a meeting?
When did Rahim get the notebook back?
What did Rahim leave in the morning?

stories.text: Roshanak works the night shift at the hospital laundry, so her husband, Olumide, takes their twins to school. On Monday one twin, Kemi, forgot her lunch box on the bus. Olumide phoned the bus company, and a driver dropped it at the school office before noon. Kemi ate her lunch in the playground with her sister.
qs: Who takes the twins to school?
What did Kemi forget on the bus?
Who dropped the lunch box at the school office?

stories.text: A goat named Oriel lived on a cliff and mocked the sheep in the valley for their thick coats. When the first snow came, Oriel shivered in the wind while the sheep slept warmly in the fold. A kind ewe let Oriel sleep beside her, and in the spring the goat showed the lambs the sweetest grass on the cliff.
qs: Where did the sheep sleep when the snow came?
Who let Oriel sleep beside her?
What did the goat show the lambs?

stories.text: On Tuesday the professor, Dr Haugland, flew from the capital to Lunvik for a conference on bees. Her suitcase was sent to the wrong airport, so she gave her first talk in the clothes she had travelled in. On Wednesday the airline sent the suitcase to her hotel by taxi. She flew home on Friday with a jar of local honey in her bag.
qs: How did the suitcase reach her hotel?
What did Dr Haugland bring home?
When did Dr Haugland fly home?

stories.text: On the allotments behind the railway, Mr Takahashi grows the biggest pumpkins. This year a boy from the next plot, Iosif, helped him water them every evening. A fox dug up two of the young plants in July, but Iosif replanted them. At the autumn show the largest pumpkin won first prize, and Mr Takahashi gave the rosette to Iosif.
qs: What dug up two of the young plants?
When were the plants dug up?
What did Mr Takahashi give to Iosif?

stories.text: The clock repairer, Bohdan Vasko, kept his workshop above a bakery on Copper Lane. On Monday a girl named Wrenna brought him a cuckoo clock that had stopped at midnight. He opened the back and found a dead moth caught in the gears. While Wrenna waited, Bohdan cleaned the wheels with a soft brush, and soon the little bird sang again. She paid him with two coins and a loaf from downstairs.
qs: What was caught in the gears?
What did Bohdan clean the wheels with?

stories.text: A heron called Maswe fished every morning at the edge of a salt marsh. A crab who lived in the mud warned her that the tide would come in early that day. Maswe laughed, because she thought crabs knew nothing about the sea. When the water rose around her long legs, she had to fly away without a single fish, and the crab waved a claw at her from his hole.
qs: Who fished at the edge of the salt marsh?
Who warned Maswe about the tide?
What did the crab wave at Maswe?

stories.text: At six in the morning the ferry left the harbour at Orvik with a cook named Pavlo in its kitchen. He baked bread while the boat crossed the strait, and by nine the loaves were cooling on a tray by the porthole. At the island of Skell the captain, Bernadine Kgosi, carried two loaves ashore for the harbour master. In the afternoon the ferry sailed back, and Pavlo washed the tray before it reached Orvik.
qs: When did the ferry leave the harbour?
Where were the loaves at nine?
Where did the captain carry the loaves ashore?

stories.text: Mrs Akintola grew tomatoes in a rooftop garden above the laundry. Her neighbour, a young drummer called Kwesi, carried water up the stairs for her every evening in two blue buckets. One night a storm bent the tallest plant, so Kwesi tied it to a broom handle with string. In August Mrs Akintola gave him a basket of tomatoes, and he made soup for the whole building.
qs: Who grew tomatoes on the roof?
What did Kwesi tie the plant to?
What did Kwesi make for the whole building?

stories.text: A young goat named Brisca wanted to cross a rope bridge over a deep gorge, but the bridge swayed in the wind. An old ram told her to wait until the wind dropped at sunset. Brisca was impatient and tried to cross at noon, and halfway over she froze. A swift landed on the rope beside her and sang until she was calm enough to walk on. That evening she thanked the bird and told the ram he had been right.
qs: Who wanted to cross the rope bridge?
When did Brisca try to cross?
What landed on the rope beside Brisca?
What did the swift do until Brisca was calm?

stories.text: Before dawn the driver, Torbjorn, took tram number nine out of the depot on Kessel Street. He drove it to the market square, where a woman left a red umbrella on the back seat. At ten o'clock a conductor named Zuleika found the umbrella and put it in the lost property box at the depot. The owner, a teacher called Mr Valente, collected it after lunch.
qs: Where did the woman leave the umbrella?
Where was the umbrella at noon?
When did Mr Valente collect the umbrella?

stories.text: At the sheep fair in Bramlow, a farmer named Deirdre Fennimore showed her best ewe to the judges. The ewe was called Pudding, and her wool had been washed the night before by Deirdre's son, Eamon. A judge with a grey beard gave Pudding a blue ribbon. On the way home Eamon tied the ribbon to the gate of the pen so that everyone in the lane would see it.
qs: Who showed her best ewe at the fair?
What did the judge give Pudding?
Where did Eamon tie the ribbon?

stories.text: Three ants found a fallen pear at the foot of a wall. The smallest ant, Tibo, said they should fetch the whole nest, but the other two began to eat at once. While they ate, a wasp landed on the pear and chased them away. Tibo came back with forty sisters, and together they drove the wasp off and carried the pear home piece by piece.
qs: What did the three ants find?
What chased the ants away from the pear?
How many sisters did Tibo bring back?

stories.text: The lighthouse school stood on a rock off the coast, and its only teacher was Miss Vanderveer. Every Friday the children rowed across from the village with their lunch in a tin. Last Friday a boy named Rafe forgot the tin on the jetty, so the keeper, Mr Sundby, rowed it over at eleven. The children ate on the lighthouse steps, and in the evening they rowed home before the lamp was lit.
qs: Who was the teacher at the lighthouse school?
Where did Rafe forget the tin?
Who rowed the tin over to the school?
When did the keeper row the tin over?

stories.text: In a small recording studio, the singer Corisande Fiske was trying to finish a song about her grandmother. Her sound engineer, Tobiah, noticed a humming noise on every take. He searched the room and found that an old fridge in the corner was causing it. Once the fridge was unplugged, Corisande sang the song in one take, and Tobiah played it back to her twice.
qs: What did Tobiah notice on every take?
What was causing the humming noise?
How many times did Tobiah play the song back?

stories.text: A tortoise named Gundo lived beside a dry riverbed, and every year he dug a deep hole to hold the rain. The meerkats laughed at him and spent the wet season playing. When the drought came, the riverbed cracked and there was nothing to drink. Gundo let the meerkats drink from his hole, and the next year they helped him dig it.
qs: Who lived beside the dry riverbed?
What did Gundo dig every year?
What did the meerkats do in the wet season?
Why was there nothing to drink?

stories.text: On Saturday morning Graziella Pace left her flat in the old town with a parcel for her brother. She first took the bus to the post office, but it was closed, so she walked on to the railway station. There she met her brother, Ottavio, under the big clock and handed him the parcel. Ottavio carried it home to his farm in the hills, and by evening the parcel was on his kitchen table.
qs: Who left her flat with a parcel?
Where did Graziella take the bus to?
Why did Graziella walk on to the railway station?
Who had the parcel after Graziella handed it over?
Where was the parcel by evening?

stories.text: Grandpa Selim fixed bicycles in the shed behind his house. One afternoon his granddaughter, Leyla, rode in with a flat tyre and a torn bag. Selim patched the tyre while Leyla sewed the bag with green thread. Before she left, he oiled her chain and told her to ride home before dark.
qs: What did Leyla sew the bag with?
What did Selim do before Leyla left?

stories.text: An owl named Ivarra was proud of her sharp eyes and boasted that nothing in the forest escaped her. One foggy night a field mouse walked right past her tree, and she did not see it. The mouse came back the next morning and politely asked whether she had enjoyed the fog. Ivarra ruffled her feathers and stayed quiet for the rest of the week.
qs: Who was proud of her sharp eyes?
When did the mouse walk past the tree?
What did the mouse ask Ivarra?
What did Ivarra do for the rest of the week?

stories.text: Early in the day a birdwatcher, Dr Rathbone, set up her telescope on the sea wall beside the salt marsh. By noon the tide had covered the mudflats, and the wading birds moved to a shingle bank. Dr Rathbone carried the telescope along the wall to a wooden hide. At dusk she walked back to her car with her notebook full and her boots soaked.
qs: Where was the telescope early in the day?
Where did the wading birds move?
What had covered the mudflats by noon?
When did Dr Rathbone walk back to her car?

stories.text: The pharmacist, Mr Tanaka, noticed that old Mrs Fairweather had not collected her medicine for three days. After closing the shop, he walked to her cottage and knocked, but nobody answered. A neighbour told him that Mrs Fairweather was staying with her daughter in Kilcarra. Mr Tanaka posted the medicine to Kilcarra the next morning, and a week later he received a thank-you card.
qs: How many days had Mrs Fairweather not collected her medicine?
What did Mr Tanaka do after closing the shop?
Who was Mrs Fairweather staying with?
What did Mr Tanaka receive a week later?

stories.text: A fox called Renko found a bell on a ribbon by the road and tied it around his neck, because he thought it made him look grand. Wherever he went the bell rang, and every rabbit heard him coming. After three hungry days, Renko gave the bell to a cow, who was glad of it. The cow's farmer, Mr Achebe, never lost her again.
qs: Who found a bell by the road?
Why did Renko tie the bell around his neck?
Who had the bell after Renko gave it away?
How many hungry days did Renko have?

stories.text: Sanjeev Menon boarded the night train in Pallam with a guitar and a small suitcase. When the train reached the border at two in the morning, an inspector checked his passport. Sanjeev fell asleep after that and left the guitar on the luggage rack when he got off at Velmora. A cleaner found it at the end of the line and sent it back on the next train, and Sanjeev collected it the following evening.
qs: When did the train reach the border?
Where did Sanjeev leave the guitar?
What did the cleaner do with the guitar?

stories.text: Mrs Oduya drove the school bus along the coast road every morning. On Wednesday a lamb was standing in the middle of the road near the quarry, and she had to stop. Two of the older pupils, Kasimir and Bettina, climbed out and gently carried the lamb back over the wall. The children arrived at school ten minutes late, and their teacher let them write about the lamb instead of doing sums.
qs: What was standing in the road?
Who carried the lamb back over the wall?
How late did the children arrive at school?

stories.text: A crow named Okke collected shiny things and hid them in a chimney pot. One day he found a gold ring in a puddle and flew home with it. A girl in the house below had been crying because she had lost that ring, and Okke heard her through the window. The next morning he dropped the ring on her windowsill, and she left him a pile of bread crusts.
qs: Where did Okke hide shiny things?
Where did Okke find the ring?
Why had the girl been crying?
What did the girl leave for Okke?

stories.text: On Monday the stone statue of a lion was in the museum courtyard. On Tuesday four workers lifted it with a crane and put it on a lorry. The lorry carried it slowly across the city to the new library, where the statue was placed beside the front door. By Wednesday afternoon children were already climbing on its back.
qs: Where was the statue on Monday?
What did the workers lift the statue with?
How many workers lifted the statue?
When were children climbing on the statue?

stories.text: The new postwoman, Signe Solberg, could not find number twelve on Marrow Hill because the sign had fallen into a hedge. A small boy who was walking his dog showed her the right gate. Signe delivered a heavy box to the house, and the owner, a retired sailor named Mr Oyelaran, opened it on the step. Inside was a model ship that his sister had built for him.
qs: Why could Signe not find number twelve?
Who showed Signe the right gate?
What had fallen into a hedge?

stories.text: A beaver named Tamsk built her dam a little higher every night. A pike in the pond complained that the water was getting too deep for him to hunt. Tamsk asked him what he would do without the pond at all, and the pike had no answer. When a dry summer came, the beaver's pond was the only water left in the valley, and the pike was glad of it.
qs: When did Tamsk build her dam higher?
What was the only water left in the valley?
What did the pike complain about?

stories.text: At sunrise the shepherd boy, Ishaan, drove forty goats from the village up to the high pasture. He spent the morning beside a spring, carving a whistle from a willow stick. In the afternoon clouds rolled over the peak, so he whistled the goats together and led them down early. By the time the rain began they were all safe in the stone fold behind his uncle's house.
qs: Who drove the goats up to the pasture?
How many goats did Ishaan drive up?
Where did Ishaan spend the morning?
Where were the goats when the rain began?

stories.text: Every Thursday a florist called Remedios Aguado left a bunch of yellow tulips at the door of the town hall. Nobody knew why until the mayor, Mr Borowski, asked her one morning. She explained that her father had been the caretaker there for forty years and had loved yellow flowers. After that the mayor put the tulips in a vase on the reception desk.
qs: Who left tulips at the town hall?
When did Remedios leave the tulips?
Who asked Remedios why she left them?
Who had been the caretaker of the town hall?
Where did the mayor put the tulips?

stories.text: A young elephant named Lomu was afraid of the water and would not bathe with the herd. A kingfisher who sat on a branch over the river told Lomu to put in one foot at a time. Each morning Lomu went in a little deeper, and the kingfisher counted the steps aloud. By the end of the month he was spraying the other calves, and they could not get him out of the river.
qs: Who was afraid of the water?
Who told Lomu to put in one foot at a time?
What did the kingfisher count aloud?
When was Lomu spraying the other calves?

stories.text: At seven o'clock Grandma Wambui put the kettle on the stove in her kitchen. Her grandson, Dov, carried it out to the garden at eight so that they could have tea under the plum tree. When a wasp came, he took the kettle back inside and left it on the windowsill. At noon it was still sitting there, cold, while Grandma Wambui slept in her chair.
qs: Where was the kettle at seven o'clock?
Who carried the kettle out to the garden?
Where did they want to have tea?
Where was the kettle at noon?
What did Grandma Wambui do at noon?

stories.text: The tailor, Radomir Hegedus, was making a wedding coat for a young man called Cosimo. Two days before the wedding, Cosimo's dog chewed one of the sleeves. Radomir worked through the night and cut a new sleeve from the last piece of the blue cloth. At the wedding nobody noticed, and Cosimo's bride, Pernille, asked who had made such a fine coat.
qs: Who was the wedding coat for?
What chewed one of the sleeves?
What did Radomir cut the new sleeve from?

stories.text: A mole called Dunstan dug a tunnel under a garden and came up in the middle of a carrot bed. The gardener's cat saw the fresh hill of earth and sat beside it all afternoon. Dunstan was too clever to come out, and he dug a second tunnel to the compost heap instead. When the cat finally went in for supper, the mole was already eating worms on the other side of the garden.
qs: Who dug a tunnel under the garden?
Where did the second tunnel go?
What was the mole eating when the cat went in?

stories.text: Arvid Torvik flew to the capital on Tuesday with a box of figs for his cousin, Sevgi. At the airport the box went through a scanner, and a guard opened it but let him keep it. Sevgi met him at the arrivals gate, and they took a taxi to her flat by the river. That evening the figs were in a bowl on her balcony, and half of them had been eaten.
qs: What did Arvid bring for his cousin?
Who opened the box at the airport?
Where were the figs that evening?

stories.text: Smoke was seen coming from the roof of the old cinema on Friday evening, and the fire crew arrived within minutes. Their captain, Riikka Lahtinen, climbed a ladder and found a bird's nest blocking the chimney. The projectionist, a quiet man named Ottorino, had lit the stove because the hall was cold. Nobody was hurt, and the film started again an hour later.
qs: Why had Ottorino lit the stove?
When did the film start again?

stories.text: A donkey named Cuthbert carried water jars for a whole village of rabbits, and he never asked for anything in return. One spring he hurt his leg on a stone and could not walk. The rabbits took turns bringing him clover and singing to him at night. When he was well again, he found that they had built him a shelter of woven reeds.
qs: Who carried water jars for the rabbits?
What did the donkey hurt his leg on?
When did the rabbits sing to him?
What had the rabbits built for him?

stories.text: In the morning the circus left the town of Durnholm in six painted wagons. The strongman, Wenceslas, drove the first wagon, and the elephant walked behind the last one. At midday they stopped by a lake so that the horses could drink. By night the whole circus had reached Faywick, and the big tent was standing in a field next to the church.
qs: How many wagons did the circus have?
What walked behind the last wagon?
Where did the circus stop at midday?
Where was the circus by night?

stories.text: Imogen Holm ran a small garage at the edge of town with her brother, Pieter. On a snowy morning a car broke down outside, and its driver, Dr Ebele, said she was late for a patient. Imogen lent her an old green van while Pieter fixed the car. By lunchtime the doctor was back, and she brought the two of them a flask of hot soup.
qs: Who ran the garage with her brother?
What did Imogen lend the doctor?
What did the doctor bring them?

stories.text: A spider named Zephra spun her web across the doorway of a garden shed. Every morning the gardener walked through it and broke it, and every evening Zephra spun it again. At last a moth told her to try the corner by the window, where nobody ever walked. Zephra moved her web there, and that night she caught more flies than ever before.
qs: Who spun a web across the doorway?
Who broke the web every morning?
Who told Zephra to try the corner?
Where did Zephra move her web?
What did Zephra catch that night?

stories.text: Chiharu wrote a letter to her pen friend in the morning and put it in the postbox at the end of her street. At four o'clock the postman emptied the box and took the letter to the sorting office. That night it travelled by train to the coast, and on Thursday it was delivered to a farmhouse where her pen friend, Sindre, lived. Sindre read it at breakfast and pinned it above his bed.
qs: Where did Chiharu put the letter?
Where was the letter after four o'clock?
What did Sindre do with the letter at breakfast?

stories.text: Mr Castellano sold ice cream from a van on the beach road all summer. One hot afternoon the freezer broke, and the ice cream began to melt. Instead of throwing it away, he gave it free to every child on the beach, and their parents bought him coffee. The next day an electrician called Faramarz repaired the freezer for nothing, because his twins had eaten three cones each.
qs: Who sold ice cream on the beach road?
Why did Faramarz repair the freezer for nothing?
What did the parents buy Mr Castellano?

stories.text: A hen named Clotilde laid her eggs in a hayloft high above the barn floor. A rat who lived under the floor wanted the eggs, but he could not climb the smooth ladder. He asked a goose to carry him up and promised to share, but the goose told Clotilde instead. Clotilde pulled the ladder up into the loft that night, and the rat never reached her eggs.
qs: Who laid eggs in the hayloft?
Who did the rat ask to carry him up?
What could the rat not climb?
When did Clotilde pull the ladder up?

stories.text: On the first day of the trip, Professor Oyebanji and her two students drove from the university to a fishing village called Penmarrow. On the second day they took a boat to a seal colony on a small island, where the students counted the pups. On the third day a storm kept them indoors at the inn, and the professor wrote her report by the fire. They drove home on the fourth day with a jar of sea glass for the department office.
qs: Who drove to the fishing village with two students?
Where did they go on the second day?
What kept them indoors on the third day?

stories.text: In a narrow street near the harbour, a bookbinder named Esperanza Ruiz repaired old books for the university. One morning a student, Ignatius, brought her a cookbook that had fallen into a bath. Esperanza dried the pages one by one with a warm iron and sewed on a new cover. When Ignatius came back, he found that she had also copied out a recipe that the water had nearly washed away.
qs: What had fallen into a bath?
What did Esperanza dry the pages with?
What had the water nearly washed away?

stories.text: The dye works stood at the bend of the Ossel River, where the water ran blue on Mondays and red on Thursdays. Its foreman, Ilkka Saran, kept the recipe book locked in a tin box under his desk. On Thursday morning a new worker named Pemba mixed the madder root too strong, and a whole bolt of cloth came out nearly black. Ilkka did not shout; he showed her how to weigh the root on the brass scale, and by evening the next bolt was a clean red.
qs: Who kept the recipe book locked away?
Who mixed the madder root too strong?
What did Ilkka show Pemba how to do?
When was the next bolt a clean red?

stories.text: A young badger named Orrin found a lantern that a miner had dropped on the hill path. He carried it into the wood to show the other animals, but its light drew the moths, who flew straight into the hot glass. An old owl, Morwen, told him that a light belongs to whoever can use it without harm. So Orrin left the lantern on a flat stone by the path, and the next day the miner came back for it.
qs: What flew into the hot glass?
What did Orrin leave on a flat stone?
Who told Orrin that a light belongs to whoever can use it?

stories.text: The barge Shearwater left the lock at Hollinsgate at six in the morning with a load of slate. By ten it had reached the boatyard at Brackwater, where the skipper, Jadwiga, stopped to mend a leaking pump. In the afternoon the barge went on to the brickworks, and the slate was unloaded onto the wharf there. Jadwiga tied up for the night beside a willow, a mile past the brickworks.
qs: Where was the barge at ten?
What did Jadwiga stop at the boatyard to do?
When did the barge leave the lock?

stories.text: Every Wednesday the chess club met in the back room of the Hazelden Library. Its oldest member, Mr Vanderhoek, had played there for forty years, and he still set up the boards before anyone else arrived. This week a quiet boy named Casimir beat him in twelve moves. Mr Vanderhoek shook his hand and gave him the club's wooden trophy, a carved knight, to keep until the next meeting.
qs: Where did the chess club meet?
How many moves did Casimir need?

stories.text: A goat called Brisket lived on a cliff above a fishing village. Each evening a gull named Pell flew up and boasted that she could see the whole sea, while the goat could only see rocks. One foggy night the gull lost her way and landed on the cliff, shivering. Brisket led her along a narrow ledge to a dry cave, and after that Pell boasted much less.
qs: What did Pell boast that she could see?
When did the gull lose her way?

stories.text: Dr Ogbonna drove up to the mountain observatory on Friday afternoon with a new lens packed in straw. She left the lens in the storeroom while she ate supper with the night assistant, Ruslan. At midnight they carried it up to the dome and fitted it to the big telescope. By dawn Ruslan had gone down to the village to sleep, but the doctor stayed in the dome writing notes.
qs: Who drove up to the observatory?
Where was the lens during supper?
When did they carry the lens to the dome?
What was the lens packed in?

stories.text: Eilif and his sister Ingeborg run a goat dairy at the top of the Skarra road. She milks the goats before sunrise, and he turns the milk into cheese in a cold stone shed. On market days their neighbour, Mrs Daskalaki, drives the cheeses to town in her blue van, because Eilif never learned to drive. In return she takes home a round of the soft cheese every week.
qs: Who drives the cheeses to town?
Why does Mrs Daskalaki drive the cheeses to town?
What does Mrs Daskalaki take home every week?

stories.text: A tortoise named Umber wanted to cross the dry riverbed before the rains came. A lizard offered to carry a message ahead to the frogs, so they would wait for him at the far bank. The lizard forgot the message as soon as it saw a fat beetle. Umber reached the far bank alone at sunset, and the frogs, who had never heard he was coming, had already gone to sleep in the reeds.
qs: Who wanted to cross the riverbed?
What did the lizard offer to do?
What made the lizard forget the message?
When did Umber reach the far bank?
Where had the frogs gone to sleep?

stories.text: The night ferry left Harrowby at nine with forty passengers and a truck full of melons. A student, Zulfiya, slept on a bench in the lounge until the ship's horn woke her at two. She went out on deck and saw the lights of Kelso harbour ahead. At four the ferry docked, and the melons were driven off before any passenger was allowed down the ramp.
qs: What was the truck full of?
What did Zulfiya do after the horn woke her?
Who saw the lights of Kelso harbour?
How many passengers were on the ferry?

stories.text: In a narrow street behind the cathedral, Matthijs builds puppets out of lime wood. His apprentice, a tall girl called Benedikta, paints their faces while he carves the hands. Last week a theatre ordered a dragon with a moving jaw, and Matthijs worked on it every night. When the dragon was finished, Benedikta tied the strings, and the theatre's director came to collect it in a handcart.
qs: Who builds puppets out of lime wood?
How did the director take the dragon away?

stories.text: Two crows, Sootfoot and Feodora, found a crust of bread on a garden wall. Sootfoot wanted to eat it at once, but Feodora said they should soak it in the birdbath to make it soft. While they argued, a squirrel ran along the wall and carried the crust up an apple tree. The crows had to share a single worm for supper.
qs: Who wanted to eat the bread at once?
Where did Feodora want to soak the bread?
What did the squirrel do with the crust?
What did the crows share for supper?

stories.text: At seven the digger driver, Anokye, started work at the sand quarry outside Redhollow. He filled the first lorry by eight, and it drove the sand to a building site in the town. Around noon a fox was seen at the edge of the pit, so the foreman stopped the digger for an hour. Anokye ate his lunch in the cab while the fox trotted away into the gorse.
qs: Where did the lorry take the sand?
What was seen at the edge of the pit?
What did Anokye do in the cab?

stories.text: Mrs Okuneye runs the post office in a village with no bank. On Tuesdays she also cuts hair in the back room, because the nearest barber is two hours away by bus. Her grandson, Kwadwo, sweeps up the hair after school and keeps the coins he earns in a jam jar. This spring he saved enough to buy a bicycle, which he now rides to deliver late letters.
qs: When does Mrs Okuneye cut hair?
Where does Kwadwo keep his coins?

stories.text: A hedgehog named Prickwell lived under the floor of a garden shed. Every night he heard a mouse gnawing at the sacks of seed above him. He climbed up and asked the mouse why she was so hungry, and she told him she was feeding seven babies in a flowerpot. After that Prickwell brought her beetles, and the gardener found his seed sacks whole again.
qs: Who lived under the floor of the shed?
What was the mouse gnawing at?
How many babies was the mouse feeding?
What did Prickwell bring the mouse?

stories.text: Zinaida's train left the capital at dawn and reached the coast before lunch. She put her suitcase in a locker at the station and walked to the harbour to see her uncle's fishing boat. In the afternoon her uncle, Bartolo, took her out past the lighthouse. They came back after dark, and she slept at his cottage instead of the hotel she had booked.
qs: Where did Zinaida put her suitcase?
Who took Zinaida out past the lighthouse?
When did the train reach the coast?
Where did Zinaida sleep that night?
What did Zinaida walk to the harbour to see?

stories.text: The driver on route nine, Mr Haraldsen, knows most of his passengers by name. On Thursday an old man left a violin case on the back seat. Mr Haraldsen kept it beside his own seat all afternoon, and at the last stop he gave it to the depot manager, Fern Mendonca. The old man came to the depot the next morning, and he played a short tune for everyone before he took the case home.
qs: What did the old man leave on the bus?
Where was the violin case all afternoon?
Who had the case after the last stop?
What did the old man do at the depot?

stories.text: A young fox, Tinder, believed he was the fastest animal in the valley. He challenged a hare, a deer and a stoat to a race around the pond. The stoat refused, saying he had a nest to guard. The deer won easily, and Tinder came last because he stopped to drink halfway round.
qs: Who challenged the others to a race?

stories.text: In the morning the postman, Dusan Brankovic, left the sorting office with a sack of parcels. He delivered the heavy ones first, to the farms along the valley road. By noon the sack held only a small box for the schoolteacher, and he carried it up the hill to the school. In the evening Dusan was back at the sorting office, where he hung the empty sack on its hook.
qs: Who left the sorting office with a sack of parcels?
What did Dusan do back at the sorting office?
What was in the sack at noon?
Where was Dusan in the evening?
Who was the small box for?

stories.text: Saleem Qureshi mends coats at a stall in the covered market. His daughter, Noorjahan, keeps the accounts in a green notebook while he works. On Saturday a customer paid with a large note, and Saleem had no change, so Noorjahan ran to the fruit seller to break it. When she came back, the customer had already gone, so they hung his coat at the front of the stall with a paper label.
qs: What did they do with the customer's coat?

stories.text: A beaver named Sallow built her dam too close to a road, and every spring the water flooded the ditches. A farmer complained to the magpie, who carried news up and down the river. The magpie told Sallow, and she moved her dam to a bend further upstream. The farmer left a pile of willow branches on the bank to thank her.
qs: Who built a dam too close to the road?
Who carried news up and down the river?
Where did Sallow move her dam?
What did the farmer leave on the bank?

stories.text: The tour group reached the old fort at ten o'clock. Their guide, Gundula, led them up to the walls, where they ate apples and looked out at the bay. Before lunch the group walked down to the market square, but two boys stayed behind to search for a lost cap. They found it in a cannon on the walls and caught up with the others at the cafe by the fountain.
qs: Who led the group up to the walls?
What did the group eat on the walls?
Where did the group walk before lunch?
What did the two boys stay behind to search for?
When did the group reach the fort?

stories.text: Old Mrs Lindgard could no longer climb the ladder to pick her pears. Her neighbour's son, a teenager named Chidozie, offered to do it on Saturday. He filled four baskets and carried them to her porch, while she made lemonade in the kitchen. She gave him the ripest basket to take home, and his mother turned the pears into jam.
qs: How many baskets did Chidozie fill?
Where did Chidozie carry the baskets?
What did Mrs Lindgard make in the kitchen?
Who turned the pears into jam?

stories.text: A bat named Quill slept all day in the bell tower of a ruined church. The pigeons below him cooed so loudly at noon that he could not rest. Quill asked them politely to move to the barn, and they laughed at him. That night he flew to the barn himself and found it full of moths, so he said nothing more to the pigeons and moved there for good.
qs: Who slept in the bell tower?
Where did Quill ask the pigeons to move?
What was the barn full of?
When did the pigeons coo loudly?

stories.text: Grandad Teoman drove his tractor to the mill at first light with ten sacks of wheat in the trailer. The miller, a woman named Dilnoza, ground the wheat while he waited outside on a bench. By mid-morning the flour was loaded back into the trailer, and Teoman took it to his daughter's bakery in the town. He was home again before the church bell rang twelve.
qs: What did Teoman do while the wheat was ground?
Where did Teoman take the flour?
How many sacks of wheat did Teoman bring?
When did Teoman drive to the mill?

stories.text: The lighthouse keeper's wife, Jorunn, painted watercolours of passing ships. A sailor named Ahanu saw one of her paintings in a shop and recognised his own boat. He walked all the way out along the breakwater to ask if he could buy it. Jorunn gave it to him for nothing, but asked him to wave from the deck the next time he sailed past.
qs: Where did Ahanu see the painting?
What did Ahanu recognise in the painting?
Who walked out along the breakwater?
What did Jorunn ask Ahanu to do?

stories.text: A spider called Inkwell spun her web across the door of a beehive. The bees could not get in, and they buzzed angrily at her. A wise old drone told them to fetch a dandelion seed, and when the wind blew the seed into the web, the threads broke. Inkwell moved her web to a thorn bush, where nobody needed to pass.
qs: Who spun a web across the door of the beehive?
Who told the bees to fetch a dandelion seed?
Where did Inkwell move her web?

stories.text: On Sunday morning the twins, Arvo and Liisa, cycled from their farm to the lake. Arvo swam out to the raft while Liisa stayed on the shore reading. At lunchtime they rode on to their aunt's house in Ebbersdorf, where they left their bicycles in the shed. In the evening their father drove over and took them home in the van, with the bicycles tied on the roof.
qs: Who swam out to the raft?
Where was Liisa while Arvo swam?
What was Liisa doing on the shore?
Where were the bicycles on the way home?

stories.text: Gwendolyn Nduka runs a repair cafe on the first Saturday of each month. People bring broken toasters, lamps and radios, and volunteers fix them for free. This month a retired electrician, Mr Lindahl, mended eleven lamps in one morning. A boy brought a toy robot that would not walk, and Gwendolyn found a dead battery inside it.
qs: How many lamps did Mr Lindahl mend?
What did Gwendolyn find inside the robot?

stories.text: A mole named Grubb dug a tunnel under a cabbage field. The rabbits complained that their burrows kept caving in. Grubb said he could not see where he was digging, so the rabbits stamped on the ground above to show him their burrows. After that he dug around them, and the rabbits let him eat the worms in their garden.
qs: Where did Grubb dig his tunnel?
Why did Grubb dig into the burrows?
What did the rabbits do to show Grubb their burrows?

stories.text: The kettle began the day on the stove in the farmhouse kitchen. At eight Seren carried it, full of tea, out to the men in the hayfield. They left it under the hedge while they worked, and at noon a dog knocked it over. Seren brought it back to the kitchen in the afternoon and set it on the windowsill to dry.
qs: Where was the kettle at the start of the day?
Who carried the kettle to the hayfield?
Where was the kettle while the men worked?
What was the kettle full of when Seren carried it out?

stories.text: Shoji Mabuchi teaches swimming at the public baths on weekday evenings. His best pupil, an eight-year-old called Delphina, was afraid of deep water until last winter. Shoji let her hold a float shaped like a duck, and every week she swam a little further from the wall. On her birthday she swam the whole length without it, while her mother clapped from the gallery.
qs: Who teaches swimming at the public baths?
What was the float shaped like?
When did Delphina swim the whole length?

stories.text: A peacock named Cobalt would not leave the stable on rainy days, because he was afraid the water would spoil his tail. A plain brown duck named Ennis told him that rain made her feathers shine. Cobalt tried a short walk to the pond in a light shower and came back dripping but no less bright. Now he walks in the yard every day, and Ennis waddles beside him.
qs: Who would not leave the stable on rainy days?
Why did Cobalt stay in the stable?
Who told Cobalt that rain made her feathers shine?
Where did Cobalt walk in the shower?

stories.text: Before sunrise the fishermen of Mawe Creek pushed their boats into the water. By nine the first boat, captained by Hamisi, had come back with a basket of crabs. The crabs were sold at the jetty to a hotel cook, who carried them up the beach in a bucket. At noon Hamisi was asleep under his boat in the shade, and his nets hung drying on the mangroves.
qs: What did the first boat bring back?
What did the hotel cook carry the crabs in?

stories.text: The school caretaker, Mr Fairbrook, found a hedgehog asleep in the boiler room on a cold morning. He put it in a cardboard box with some leaves and phoned the animal shelter. A vet named Dr Kaminska came at lunchtime and said the hedgehog was too thin to sleep through the winter. She took it to the shelter, where it was fed on cat food until spring.
qs: What did Mr Fairbrook put the hedgehog in?
What was the hedgehog fed on at the shelter?

stories.text: A field mouse named Pipkin stored acorns in an old boot at the edge of the orchard. A jay watched him every day and stole one acorn each morning. When Pipkin noticed the pile getting smaller, he filled the top of the boot with pebbles. The jay pecked at a pebble, hurt his beak, and never came back.
qs: Where did Pipkin store his acorns?
What did Pipkin fill the top of the boot with?

stories.text: The map started the trip in Ileana's rucksack. At the first hut she gave it to her cousin Corneliu, who was leading the walk that afternoon. Corneliu dropped it by a stream, and a shepherd named Gavril picked it up and carried it to the second hut. When the cousins arrived there at dusk, Gavril handed the map back to Corneliu over a bowl of soup.
qs: Where was the map at the start of the trip?
Who had the map after Ileana gave it away?
What did Gavril do at the second hut?
Who carried the map to the second hut?
When did the cousins arrive at the second hut?

stories.text: Every autumn the beekeeper, Thaddeus Mwangi, takes his honey to the county show. This year his jar of heather honey won second prize, and a judge asked where his hives were. He told her they stood on a moor above the village, beside a broken stone wall. The first prize went to his cousin, Tahmina, who keeps her bees in an apple orchard.
qs: Who takes his honey to the county show?
Where do the hives of Thaddeus stand?
What did the judge ask Thaddeus?

stories.text: A frog called Bellwether lived in a rain barrel behind a toolshed. He told every passing insect that the barrel was the biggest lake in the world. One day a duck let him ride on her back to the river, and Bellwether was so frightened by the size of it that he hid under a lily pad. When he got home, he stopped boasting and started asking visitors about the places they had seen.
qs: Who lived in the rain barrel?
What did the duck let Bellwether do?
Who took Bellwether to the river?
Where did Bellwether hide at the river?
What did Bellwether do when he got home?

stories.text: The travelling theatre packed up in Zelin at midnight and loaded its van. Early the next morning the company drove south over the pass, and at noon they stopped in a village where the puppeteer, Stanimir, bought cheese. By evening they had reached the seaside town of Corvella. The puppets spent that night in their trunks in the hotel garage, and the show opened in the town square the following day.
qs: When did the theatre pack up?
Where were the puppets that night?
What did the company do early the next morning?

stories.text: Perpetua works the night shift at a hospital laundry. When she comes home at seven, her husband, Bram, is just leaving for his job at the railway yard. They share breakfast at the kitchen table for twenty minutes, and when he has to rush, he leaves her a note on the fridge. On Sundays neither of them works, so they walk their dog by the canal.
qs: Who works at the railway yard?
What does Bram leave on the fridge?
What do Perpetua and Bram do on Sundays?

stories.text: At the ropewalk on Tarry Lane, the foreman, Dragomir Ilesco, measured each length of hemp with a knotted cord. His niece Njeri twisted the strands while he walked backward down the long shed. By noon the rope was finished, and it was coiled onto a cart that took it to the harbour. That evening a ship's mate named Fergal paid for it with three silver coins.
qs: Who measured each length of hemp?
Where did the cart take the rope?
How many silver coins did Fergal pay?

stories.text: A hedgehog named Tibble kept a store of beechnuts in a hollow log. One autumn a jay, Corvina, asked to borrow a handful and promised to pay them back in spring. The hedgehog agreed, but he watched her bury them all over the meadow and forget where. In spring the meadow was full of little beech trees, and Corvina brought him a whole branch of nuts from the oldest one.
qs: Who kept a store of beechnuts?
Who asked to borrow a handful?
What did Corvina do with the nuts?
What was the meadow full of in spring?

stories.text: Early on Tuesday the lock keeper, Anselm Kovari, opened the upper gates of Thorrel Lock to let a barge through. The barge, which carried bricks, dropped slowly in the chamber until it sat level with the lower river. Anselm then walked to the cottage for breakfast while his daughter Ermengarde closed the gates behind it. By midday the barge had reached the brickyard at Penner's Quay, and its bricks were unloaded onto the wharf.
qs: What did Ermengarde close behind the barge?
Where did Anselm walk for breakfast?
Where were the bricks at the end?

stories.text: Mrs Okunade runs a market garden behind the railway embankment. Every Friday she picks lettuces before sunrise, and her neighbour, a retired postman called Timur, helps her wash them in a tin bath. Because the frost came early this year, the beans were covered with old sheets. On Saturday the lettuces were sold at the corner stall by her son Kobina, who kept the money in his apron.
qs: Why were the beans covered with old sheets?
Who had the money on Saturday?

stories.text: Two goats, Bolek and Doruk, shared a field with a broken fence. Bolek wanted to go through the gap to eat the farmer's cabbages, but Doruk said the gap was there to let the wind through, not goats. While they argued, a crow flew down and ate the best cabbage herself. The farmer mended the fence that afternoon, and the goats never got a single leaf.
qs: Who wanted to go through the gap?
What did Bolek want to eat?
What did the farmer do that afternoon?
When did the farmer mend the fence?

stories.text: At dawn Soraya Khoury set out from the lighthouse with a basket of eggs for her aunt. She followed the cliff path past the signal hut, where she left two eggs for the coastguard, Mr Nyqvist. By mid-morning she was at her aunt's farm on Skua Head, and the basket was put on the kitchen table. In the afternoon she walked home along the beach instead.
qs: Who set out from the lighthouse?
What did Soraya carry for her aunt?
Where was the basket in the afternoon?

stories.text: The glassblower, Ifeyinwa Okonkwo, heated a gob of glass until it glowed orange. Her apprentice, a tall boy named Kazimierz, blew through the long pipe while she turned it. The bowl they made was set in the cooling oven overnight. In the morning a customer, Mrs Tveit, collected it and carried it home wrapped in newspaper.
qs: Where was the bowl set overnight?
What was the bowl wrapped in?

stories.text: A tortoise named Hippolyte was asked by the frogs to judge a singing contest at the pond. The bullfrog sang loudest, but a tiny tree frog, Lili, sang the sweetest song. Hippolyte took so long to decide that the moon set and every frog fell asleep. When they woke, he gave the prize, a shiny pebble, to the heron, who had been the only one listening.
qs: Who was asked to judge the contest?
What did every frog do when the moon set?

stories.text: On Sunday morning the grey pony, Thistle, was led from her stable to the outdoor ring. Madame Corbeau taught three children to trot there until eleven. After the lesson a girl called Liesbet rode Thistle down the lane to the paddock, and the pony stayed there all afternoon. At dusk the groom, Chidubem, brought her back to the stable.
qs: Who taught the children to trot?
How many children did Madame Corbeau teach?
Where was Thistle in the afternoon?
Where was Thistle at the end?

stories.text: The print shop on Ferrow Street was busy because the town election was only two days away. Mr Hoogeveen set the type for the posters by hand, letter by letter, while his partner, Erdem Demir, inked the press. A boy from the bakery next door was paid to fold the leaflets. The posters were hung in every shop window by Thursday.
qs: Why was the print shop busy?
Who set the type for the posters?
What was the boy paid to do?

stories.text: A fox named Garnock found a bell tied to a gate and thought it would make him important. He wore it around his neck to the river, but every rabbit heard him coming and hid. Hungry and cross, he gave the bell to a lamb, Merrin, who liked the sound. Now the shepherd always knows where Merrin is, and the fox hunts quietly again.
qs: Where was the bell at first?
What did the rabbits do when they heard him?
Who had the bell at the end?
What did Garnock wear around his neck?

stories.text: The seed bank sits inside a hill above the village of Kestrup. At nine o'clock a packet of barley seeds was taken from the cold vault by the keeper, Dr Nakashima, and carried to the counting room. There her assistant, Petronella, counted exactly two hundred seeds onto a tray. In the afternoon the tray went to the greenhouse, where the seeds were sown in wet sand.
qs: Where does the seed bank sit?
Who took the barley seeds from the vault?
What did Petronella count onto a tray?
Where was the tray in the afternoon?
When was the packet taken from the vault?

stories.text: Grandpa Mikolaj lost his reading glasses on Saturday. His granddaughter Ayasha looked under the sofa and in the bread bin, but they were not there. In the end the dog, Pickle, was found asleep on them in his basket. Mikolaj laughed, cleaned the glasses with his scarf, and read the paper to the whole family.
qs: What did Mikolaj clean the glasses with?
Who was asleep on the glasses?

stories.text: A mole named Ruggero dug a tunnel under the garden wall to reach the onion bed. Halfway along he met a worm, Wiggit, who complained that the tunnel had split her home in two. Ruggero felt sorry, so he dug her a new room with a round ceiling. The worm was so pleased that she showed him the softest soil, and he reached the onions by sunset.
qs: Who dug a tunnel under the garden wall?
What did Ruggero want to reach?
What did Ruggero dig for Wiggit?
When did Ruggero reach the onions?

stories.text: Wirrin caught the early bus from Moorbridge to visit her brother in the city. She left her umbrella on the bus, and the driver, Mr Quaye, took it to the depot.
