That afternoon her brother, Jarrah, drove her to the depot, where she found the umbrella on a shelf in the lost property room. She was back in Moorbridge by nine that night.
qs: Who took the umbrella to the depot?
Where was the umbrella in the afternoon?
Who drove Wirrin to the depot?
Where was Wirrin by nine that night?

stories.text: When the power went out on Damson Row, the baker, Oluwaseun, lit the old wood oven in his yard. Neighbours brought him their dough, and he baked twelve loaves before dark. A nurse named Brigid carried two of them to the old people's home on the hill. The lights came back on at midnight, but by then the bread was gone.
qs: Who lit the old wood oven?
What did the neighbours bring the baker?
Who carried two loaves to the old people's home?
When did the lights come back on?

stories.text: A young otter named Flitch wanted to be the fastest swimmer in the stream. Every morning he raced the trout, and every morning he lost. One day an old pike, Grizel, told him to stop racing and start watching. Flitch learned where the fish rested in the shade, and soon he caught more than any otter in the stream.
qs: Who wanted to be the fastest swimmer?
Who did Flitch race every morning?
Who told Flitch to stop racing?
What did Grizel tell Flitch to start doing?

stories.text: Before breakfast Hiroko filled the copper kettle at the pump in the yard. She hung it over the campfire, and at eight o'clock she poured tea for the surveyors. At noon the kettle was packed onto the mule with the tents, and by evening the whole camp had moved to the ridge above Lake Ostra. There the kettle hung over a new fire while the surveyors studied their maps.
qs: What did Hiroko pour for the surveyors?
Where was the kettle at noon?
Where was the camp by evening?

stories.text: Wieslawa drives the mobile library van to three villages every Wednesday. In the first village a farmer, Mr Brannigan, returned a book about bees that was a month late. A girl named Torborg borrowed it straight away, because her class was studying bees. Wieslawa did not charge the farmer a fine, but she asked him for a jar of honey instead.
qs: Who drives the mobile library van?
How many villages does the van visit?
Who returned the book about bees?
Why did Torborg borrow the book?
What did Wieslawa ask for instead of a fine?

stories.text: A sparrow, Tweedle, built her nest in the mouth of a stone lion on the town hall. The mayor's cat, Cinder, tried to reach it every day but could not climb the smooth stone. One windy night the nest blew down into the fountain, and Tweedle thought all was lost. In the morning the cat carried the dripping nest back up the stairs to the balcony, and Tweedle forgave him.
qs: Who built a nest in the stone lion?
Where did the nest blow down?
Where was the nest at the end?
What did Cinder do in the morning?

stories.text: Old Mr Zawadzki kept his rowing boat in a shed by the canal. On Monday Mr Zawadzki's grandson, Ilyas, borrowed it and rowed to the island to fish. A storm came up, so Ilyas tied the boat to the jetty at the inn and walked home. The next morning Mr Zawadzki found his boat missing from the shed, and Ilyas had to walk back to the inn to fetch it.
qs: What did Ilyas go to the island to do?
Where was the boat the next morning?
Why did Ilyas tie the boat at the inn?

stories.text: The new cook at the school canteen, Pavlina, burned the rice on her first day. The head teacher, Mr Ikeogu, ate it anyway and said it tasted smoky. On the second day she made a fish stew, and the children asked for more. By Friday the caretaker, Yoram, was coming in early just to smell her bread.
qs: What did Mr Ikeogu say about the rice?
What did Pavlina make on the second day?
Who came in early to smell the bread?
When did Pavlina burn the rice?

stories.text: A crab named Tolliver lived under a flat rock and never let anyone visit. When the tide went far out, his rock dried in the sun and grew hot. A family of shrimps let him shelter in their pool, though he had once chased them away. After that the crab shared his rock with anyone who needed it.
qs: Who lived under a flat rock?
What happened to the rock when the tide went out?
Who let Tolliver shelter in their pool?
What did the crab do after that?

stories.text: At seven the postwoman, Ngozi, collected a parcel from the sorting office. She took it first to the chemist on Wicker Square, but the shop was shut. She carried it on to the library, where the librarian, Mr Fitzwilliam, signed for it and kept it behind the desk. Later the chemist, Hermione Ekberg, fetched her parcel from the library on her way home.
qs: Where did Ngozi take the parcel first?
Where was the parcel kept at the library?
Who had the parcel at the end?

stories.text: Every spring Daiki and his sister Emi paint their father's fishing boat. This year they chose bright yellow, because the old green had faded to grey. Their father, a quiet man named Shinobu, called the boat Sunflower when he saw it. The boat went back into the water on Monday, and the whole harbour came to look.
qs: Who helps Daiki paint the boat?
What colour did they choose this year?
Why did they choose a new colour?
What did Shinobu call the boat?
When did the boat go back into the water?

stories.text: A field mouse named Odette found a ripe strawberry too heavy to carry. She asked a beetle, a snail and a lizard to help her. The beetle and the snail were too busy, but the lizard, Skitter, pulled it on a leaf all the way to her burrow. That night Odette and Skitter ate the strawberry together, and the beetle smelled it from his log.
qs: Who helped Odette move the strawberry?
How did Skitter move the strawberry?
Where did the strawberry end up?
What did Odette and Skitter do that night?

stories.text: On market day Emilio loaded his cart with cheeses at the dairy before dawn. He sold half of them in the square at Valtorre by ten, then drove on to the fair at Corrow Hollow. A cheese that rolled off the cart was found by a girl named Folake, who returned it at the fair. Emilio gave her the cheese as a reward, and she took it home to her grandmother.
qs: What did Emilio load his cart with?
Where did Emilio sell half the cheeses?
Who found the cheese that rolled off the cart?
Where was the lost cheese at the end?
What did Emilio give Folake as a reward?

stories.text: The footbridge over the Lanner Brook was closed on Tuesday after a beam was found to be rotten. Council workers, led by an engineer named Zarina Owusu, replaced the beam within three days. During the repairs walkers were sent across the ford at Ashwold. The bridge reopened on Friday with a new handrail painted blue.
qs: Where were walkers sent during the repairs?
What colour was the new handrail?

stories.text: A bear named Bramwell woke too early from his winter sleep and found the forest still covered in snow. He knocked at the squirrel's tree, but the squirrel, Cobnut, would only give him three acorns. The bear grumbled and went back into his den. When he woke again the snow had melted, and Cobnut had left a whole pile of acorns at his door.
qs: Whose tree did Bramwell knock at?
How many acorns did Cobnut give at first?
What did the bear do after he grumbled?
Where did Cobnut leave a pile of acorns?

stories.text: At six in the morning a crate of oranges was lifted onto the ferry at Port Selwyn. The ferryman, Ferdinand Mbala, stacked it beside the wheelhouse. When the ferry docked at Corran Island at noon, a shopkeeper named Mrs Teague wheeled the crate up the slipway to her store. By evening the oranges were sitting in a bowl on her counter, priced at a penny each.
qs: Who stacked the crate beside the wheelhouse?
Where was the crate during the crossing?
When did the ferry dock at Corran Island?
Who wheeled the crate up the slipway?
Where were the oranges by evening?

stories.text: Nasrullah works nights as a security guard at the museum. At two in the morning he heard a noise in the hall of fossils, and he crept in with his torch. It was only a pigeon that had flown in through a broken skylight. Nasrullah caught it in his cap and let it go from the front steps, and the director, Mrs Vasquez, had the skylight mended the next day.
qs: Where did Nasrullah hear a noise?
What did Nasrullah catch the pigeon in?

stories.text: A proud rooster named Albrecht believed his crowing made the sun rise. One morning he had a sore throat and could not make a sound. The sun rose anyway, and the hens, led by a sensible hen called Gwenllian, went on with their work. After that the rooster crowed only because he liked it.
qs: Who believed his crowing made the sun rise?
Why could Albrecht not crow one morning?
What did the sun do anyway?
Who crowed only because he liked it?

stories.text: Before lunch the ward sister, Honorine, found a teddy bear left on a bed in the children's ward. She took it to the front desk, where a porter, Lwazi, put it in the lost box. At four o'clock a mother came looking for it, but the box had already been carried down to the basement. Lwazi fetched the bear from the basement, and the little boy, Caspian, fell asleep holding it on the way home.
qs: Where was the teddy bear first?
What did Lwazi fetch from the basement?
Where was the box at four o'clock?
Who fell asleep holding the bear?

stories.text: The two neighbours on Quarry Road, Mr Magalhaes and Mrs Olawale, argued every summer about a pear tree that grew on the line between their gardens. This year the tree gave so many pears that neither of them could eat them all. Mrs Olawale made jam, Mr Magalhaes made a pear cake, and they swapped them over the fence. The argument was forgotten until the leaves fell.
qs: What did the neighbours argue about?
What did the tree give so many of this year?
Where did they swap the jam and the cake?

stories.text: A young eagle named Seraphine was afraid to leave her nest on the cliff. Her brother, Taavi, flew out every morning and came back boasting. One day a gust blew Seraphine off the ledge, and she found that her wings already knew what to do. By the end of summer she flew higher than Taavi, though she never boasted about it.
qs: Who was afraid to leave her nest?
What blew Seraphine off the ledge?
When did Seraphine fly higher than Taavi?

stories.text: The class from Wendleby School left by coach at eight to visit the paper mill. Their teacher, Mr Adeyinka, counted twenty children onto the coach and twenty off again. At the mill each child made a sheet of paper, and the sheets were hung to dry in the loft. In the afternoon the coach took them to the river meadow for lunch, but the paper stayed at the mill until it was posted to the school a week later.
qs: How many children were counted onto the coach?
Where were the sheets hung to dry?
Where were the children in the afternoon?

stories.text: A woman named Zofia keeps bees on the roof of her block of flats. Her neighbour below, a taxi driver called Abel, was afraid of them at first. Then Zofia gave him a jar of honey, and he started bringing her old flower pots from the market. Now there are lavender bushes all along the roof, and the bees hardly ever leave.
qs: What does Zofia keep on the roof?
Who was afraid of the bees at first?
What did Abel bring from the market?
What grows all along the roof now?

stories.text: A raven named Ulric stole a silver spoon from a picnic and hid it in an empty chimney. A jackdaw, Jink, saw where he hid it and moved it to her own nest. When Ulric found the chimney empty, he accused the magpies, who had done nothing. The magpies chased him around the church tower until the jackdaw, ashamed, dropped the spoon on the church step for its owner.
qs: Where did Ulric hide the spoon?
Who moved the spoon to her own nest?
Where was the spoon at the end?

stories.text: On the first day of the walk, Wojtek and his friend Nadira carried a heavy map case from the youth hostel at Brennock to the shepherd's hut on the moor. They slept in the hut, and in the night it rained so hard that the map case leaked. The next morning they dried the maps on a wall in the sun. By dusk they had reached the inn at Saltcombe, where the map case hung by the fire.
qs: Who carried the map case with Wojtek?
What did they dry in the sun?
What happened to the map case in the night?
Where were the maps the next morning?
Where was the map case at the end?

stories.text: Mr Grzybowski mends bicycles in a railway arch near the station. On Monday a schoolgirl, Ishani, brought in a bike with a bent wheel, and he promised it for Wednesday. On Tuesday his cousin Zsolt straightened the wheel while Mr Grzybowski replaced the chain. Ishani rode the bicycle home on Wednesday, ringing the new bell he had added for free.
qs: What did Ishani ring as she rode home?
Who brought in a bike with a bent wheel?
When did Ishani ride the bicycle home?

stories.text: Deep under the hill at Brannock Farm, the cheesemaker, Wendeline Ferrand, turned the wheels of cheese every morning. Her apprentice, a quiet boy named Mawuli, brushed salt water onto the rinds. On Thursday a buyer from the city tasted a slice and ordered twelve wheels. They were wrapped in waxed cloth and loaded onto a van before dark.
qs: Who turned the wheels of cheese every morning?
What did Mawuli brush onto the rinds?
How many wheels did the buyer order?
What were the wheels wrapped in?

stories.text: A badger called Brackwell dug a new burrow under a hawthorn hedge. Before he had finished, a family of rabbits moved into the front room and refused to leave. Brackwell did not argue with them. Instead he dug a second door at the back, and that winter the rabbits kept the front of the burrow warm while he slept snugly at the far end.
qs: Where did Brackwell dig the burrow?
Who moved into the front room?
What did Brackwell dig at the back?
What did the rabbits keep warm?

stories.text: The mountain bus left Vellara at six in the morning with eleven passengers. Its driver, Mr Saito, stopped at the dairy halfway up to collect the milk churns. At the pass a hiker named Sigrun got off with her map, and the bus went down the far side to the market town of Ostrell. By noon the churns had been unloaded, and Mr Saito was drinking coffee in the square.
qs: When did the bus leave Vellara?
What did the driver collect at the dairy?
Where was Mr Saito at noon?

stories.text: Mrs Ndukwe carried her husband's old boots to the cobbler's in Tannerby. The cobbler, a tall man named Cathal, found that both soles had worn through. He stitched new leather soles onto them while she waited, and he polished the toes until they shone. She paid him four coins and wrapped the boots in brown paper for the walk home.
qs: Who carried the boots to the cobbler's?
Who stitched new soles onto the boots?
What did Mrs Ndukwe wrap the boots in?

stories.text: In a dry summer a tortoise named Pembe found the last puddle in the valley. A proud stork, Altair, said the water was his because he had seen it first from the sky. Pembe answered that the sky did not drink. While they argued, the sun dried the puddle, and both of them had to walk to the river after all.
qs: Who found the last puddle in the valley?
Who said the water was his?
Why did the stork say the water was his?
Where did both of them have to walk?

stories.text: Every morning at seven, Dr Rasmusdottir climbed the path from the village to the weather station above Skarvik. There she read the rain gauge and wrote the numbers in a green notebook. At ten a radio call came from the harbour master, Gergely, who wanted to know about the wind. She told him a storm was coming, so he kept the fishing boats in port, and in the afternoon she walked back down to the village.
qs: Who climbed the path to the weather station?
Where did Dr Rasmusdottir write the numbers?
When did the radio call come?
Who wanted to know about the wind?
Where did Dr Rasmusdottir walk in the afternoon?

stories.text: In the square at Hembury there is a hat shop run by two sisters, Esmeralda and Amparo Quirino. Esmeralda steams the felt and shapes it on wooden blocks, while Amparo sews the ribbons on. Last week a bride's mother ordered a wide blue hat for the wedding. The hat was finished on Friday, and the shop boy, Hipolito, delivered it in a round box.
qs: What did the bride's mother order?

stories.text: A young otter, Sisu, was afraid of the deep pool below the weir. Each evening his grandmother floated on her back near the bank and called to him. One night a heron stood on the bank where Sisu usually sat, so he slipped into the water to get away from it. By morning he was swimming beside his grandmother as if he had never been afraid.
qs: Who was afraid of the deep pool?
What did his grandmother do each evening?
What stood on the bank where Sisu usually sat?
Why did Sisu slip into the water?

stories.text: The cafe at the end of Sandle Pier opens at dawn for the fishermen. Its owner, Rasha, bakes bread rolls in the back kitchen before anyone arrives. At midday the tourists come off the ferry, and her nephew Isandro carries trays out to the tables on the deck. In the evening the chairs are stacked inside and the shutters are locked.
qs: Where does Rasha bake the rolls?
When do the tourists come off the ferry?
Who carries trays out to the tables?
What are stacked inside in the evening?

stories.text: Mr Uzoma grows young oak and birch trees at a forest nursery outside Lindqvarn. In April his daughter, Chidinma, planted three hundred acorns in a shaded bed by the stream. The seedlings came up in May, and a man from the council came to count them. In autumn they were dug up and taken to the burnt hillside, where volunteers planted them in the rain.
qs: Who grows young oak and birch trees?
Where did Chidinma plant the acorns?
Who came to count the seedlings?
Where were the seedlings taken in autumn?

stories.text: A crow named Ebon collected shiny buttons and kept them in a nest at the top of a chimney. When the family below lit their first fire of the year, smoke poured up through the nest. Ebon flew out coughing, and the buttons fell down the chimney into the hearth. The little girl of the house, Freya, found them in the ashes and sewed them onto her coat.
qs: What poured up through the nest?
Where did Freya find the buttons?
What did Freya do with the buttons?

stories.text: Early on Monday the sailmaker, Ambrose Nkemelu, unrolled a torn mainsail across the floor of the sail loft. He had fetched it the evening before from the yacht Merrow, which was tied up in the marina. All morning he stitched a canvas patch over the tear with a curved needle. At three o'clock his assistant, Clea, rowed the sail back out to the yacht.
qs: What did the sailmaker unroll across the floor?
Where was the yacht tied up?
What did he stitch over the tear?
When did Clea row the sail back to the yacht?
Who rowed the sail back out to the yacht?

stories.text: Old Mr Fitzgibbon could no longer reach the apples on his tallest tree. His neighbour, a nurse called Divya, brought a ladder over the fence one Saturday. While she picked, he held the basket steady, and her two sons carried the full baskets to his shed. In return he gave them a jar of apple jelly every week until Christmas.
qs: What could Mr Fitzgibbon no longer reach?
Who brought a ladder over the fence?
What did Mr Fitzgibbon hold steady?
Who carried the full baskets to his shed?
What did he give them every week?

stories.text: Two squirrels, Kestrin and Moll, shared an old elm at the edge of the park. Kestrin hid his nuts in a hundred places and forgot most of them, while Moll kept hers in one hole in the trunk. One winter a woodpecker drilled into the trunk and ate everything in Moll's hole. That spring Kestrin shared the few nuts he could still find, and his forgotten ones grew into young trees all over the park.
qs: Who hid his nuts in a hundred places?
Where did Moll keep her nuts?
Whose hole did the woodpecker empty?
What did the forgotten nuts grow into?

stories.text: On Saturday the Monteiro family left their flat in the city and drove to the lake. At the boathouse they hired a rowing boat, and Ernesto, the eldest, rowed them across to a small island. They ate lunch under a willow there while their dog, Bosun, chased ducks along the shore. In the evening they rowed back, returned the boat, and drove home in the dark.
qs: Where did the family hire a rowing boat?
Who rowed them across to the island?
What did Bosun chase along the shore?

stories.text: A library van that visits the hill villages broke down near Ashcombe on Tuesday. Its driver, Mrs Stavrou, telephoned the garage, and a mechanic named Esteban arrived within the hour. While he mended the fan belt, she lent books to the children who had gathered round. The van reached its last village two hours late, but nobody seemed to mind.
qs: What did Mrs Stavrou do while he worked?
When did the van break down?

stories.text: A field mouse named Tansy lived beneath a scarecrow in a wheat field. Every year the farmer replaced the scarecrow's straw, and every year Tansy lined her nest with the old straw. One autumn the farmer brought a cat instead of new straw. That night Tansy packed her seeds into the scarecrow's hat and moved to the hedge, where the cat never thought to look.
qs: What did Tansy line her nest with?
What did the farmer bring instead of new straw?
Where did Tansy pack her seeds?

stories.text: At eight the post van dropped three sacks at the village shop in Tregarth. The postwoman, Dobrawa, sorted the letters on the counter and set off on her bicycle. She went first to the farms along the river, then up to the vicarage, and she ate her sandwiches on the bench by the war memorial. By four o'clock her bag was empty and her bicycle was back in the shed behind the shop.
qs: When did the post van drop the sacks?
What did Dobrawa set off on?
Where did she eat her sandwiches?
Where was her bicycle by four o'clock?

stories.text: Ms Horvath teaches music at the school in Wrexley. Before the spring concert she lent her own violin to a pupil, Chukwudi, because his had a cracked neck. The cracked one was sent to a repairer in town, who glued it and fitted new strings. On the night of the concert Chukwudi played a solo, and his grandparents clapped from the front row.
qs: Who teaches music at the school?
Who did Ms Horvath lend her violin to?
Why did Ms Horvath lend her violin?
What did Chukwudi play on the night of the concert?
Who clapped from the front row?

stories.text: A goat named Brimble and a donkey named Osk shared a field behind the farmhouse. When the gate blew open in a gale, the goat wanted to run to the cabbage garden, but the donkey said the road was dangerous. The goat went alone and was chased all the way back by the farm dog, Sabre. After that Brimble listened when Osk spoke, and Osk let him stand on his back to reach the apple branches.
qs: Where did the goat want to run?
Who said the road was dangerous?
What did Osk let Brimble do?

stories.text: On Wednesday morning Mr Abernathy's class took the train from Corrin to the coast. They spent the morning at the tide pools, where a ranger named Nasrin showed them starfish and crabs. After lunch they visited the lighthouse and climbed its hundred and twelve steps. The train brought them home at six, and parents were waiting on the platform.
qs: Whose class took the train to the coast?
Where did the class spend the morning?
Who showed them starfish and crabs?
What did they visit after lunch?
What did they climb at the lighthouse?

stories.text: At the Pewter Jug cafe the cook, Vojtech, starts the soup at five in the morning. His sister Zelda takes the orders and writes them on a slate. On Sundays the cafe is closed, so Vojtech goes fishing on the reservoir with his friend Okello. Whatever they catch is cooked for Monday's lunch.
qs: When does Vojtech start the soup?
Who writes the orders on a slate?
What does Zelda write the orders on?

stories.text: A snail named Pellam decided to visit his cousin on the far side of the garden path. A blackbird, Merle, offered to carry him in her beak, but Pellam did not trust her. He crossed the path slowly through a whole afternoon, and the blackbird kept watch so that no thrush could reach him. When he arrived he thanked her, and the two have been friends ever since.
qs: Who decided to visit his cousin?
What did Merle offer to carry him in?
How long did Pellam take to cross the path?

stories.text: Captain Kabongo's ferry left Tarbet harbour at nine with a cargo of flour and two cars. Halfway across the sound the fog came down, and she slowed the engines and sounded the horn. The ferry reached the island an hour late, where young Rhodri was waiting on the slipway with a tractor. By the afternoon the flour was in the island bakery and the ferry was on its way back.
qs: When did the ferry leave the harbour?
What came down halfway across the sound?
Who was waiting on the slipway?
Where was the flour by the afternoon?

stories.text: Every year the residents of Thimble Court sign a card for their caretaker, Mr Zungu. This year Mrs Holloway took the card from door to door, and forty neighbours signed it in the hallway. The children drew a picture of his red toolbox on the back. On his birthday they left it on his desk in the boiler room, with a cake from the corner bakery.
qs: What did the residents sign for their caretaker?
Who took the card from door to door?
Where did the neighbours sign the card?
How many neighbours signed the card?
Where did they leave the card?

stories.text: A frog named Bulmer lived in a rain barrel behind a greenhouse. Every night he sang so loudly that the gardener's cat, Pashmina, could not sleep. The cat complained to the moths, and the moths complained to the moon, but nobody could stop the frog. In the end a dry week quieted him, because the barrel ran low and he went off to find a pond.
qs: Who did the cat complain to?
What quieted the frog in the end?
Why did Bulmer go off to find a pond?

stories.text: On the morning of the fair, Grandpa Anand packed his jars of honey into a wooden crate. His granddaughter, Golnar, carried the crate to the car while he locked the hives. They drove to the fairground at Wetherby Green and set up a table beside the cider tent. Golnar watched the stall at lunchtime while her grandfather walked round the show ring, and by evening every jar was sold.
qs: Where did Grandpa Anand pack his jars of honey?
Who carried the crate to the car?
When did Golnar watch the stall?
Where did her grandfather walk at lunchtime?

stories.text: Dr Ngata is the only vet on the island of Skerra. When a ewe at Hollins Farm had trouble with her lamb, the farmer, Ciaran, phoned her at midnight. She drove across the island in her old jeep and helped the lamb into the world. The farmer's wife made her tea in the kitchen, and the lamb was named Midnight.
qs: Who is the only vet on the island?
When did Ciaran phone the vet?
How did Dr Ngata cross the island?
What did Dr Ngata help into the world?

stories.text: A young fox, Rufina, wanted to learn to climb like the cats in the village. Each night she practised on the woodpile behind the inn, and each night she fell off. The innkeeper's old tomcat, Barnaby, watched her from the windowsill and finally came down to show her how to use her claws. By midsummer she could reach the roof of the woodshed, though she never did learn to come down gracefully.
qs: Who wanted to learn to climb?
Who watched her from the windowsill?
What did Barnaby show her how to use?
When could she reach the roof of the woodshed?

stories.text: On Monday a parcel of rare seeds left a seed bank in the north and travelled by train to the capital. On Tuesday it was flown to a mountain town, and a courier named Dawit carried it by motorbike to the research garden. There the head gardener, Mrs Llewellyn, signed for the parcel at the gate. By Friday the seeds were planted in the glasshouse, each in its own labelled pot.
qs: How did the parcel travel to the capital?
Who carried the parcel by motorbike?
Where did Mrs Llewellyn sign for the parcel?

stories.text: The clock on the bus station in Dunmarra stopped at twenty past four one windy night. In the morning the town clerk, Ms Akinyemi, sent for a clockmaker, Mr Bergkvist, who arrived on the noon bus. He climbed the ladder inside the tower and found that a pigeon had built a nest against the hands. He moved the nest to a box on the roof, oiled the gears, and the clock was going again by tea time.
qs: Who arrived on the noon bus?
What had built a nest against the hands?

stories.text: A beaver named Osgood built a dam that turned the meadow into a pond. The moorhens loved the pond, but an old vole, Hepzibah, grumbled because her tunnels had flooded. Osgood felt sorry for her and built her a dry room in the side of his lodge. Now the vole sleeps above the water and the moorhens nest in the reeds outside.
qs: What did the dam turn the meadow into?

stories.text: At dawn the herder, Batzorig, drove his goats from the village to the high pasture. He spent the day on a rock above the stream, carving a spoon and watching for wolves. When the sun dropped behind the ridge, he whistled for his dog and brought the goats down again. By nightfall the goats were in their pen behind the house, and Batzorig was eating noodles by the stove.
qs: Where did Batzorig drive his goats at dawn?
Where were the goats by nightfall?
What was Batzorig doing by the stove?

stories.text: The footbridge over the river in Kilnsey was painted by volunteers last weekend. The paint was donated by a hardware shop owned by Mr Banerjee, and the brushes were lent by the primary school. A retired engineer, Mrs Adewale, checked every bolt before the painting began. The work was finished on Sunday afternoon, and the bridge is now bright green.
qs: What was lent by the primary school?

stories.text: On the roof of the railway station lived two pigeons, Vesper and Cobble. Vesper boasted that she could fly to the next town faster than the express train. Cobble did not believe her, so they agreed on a race the next morning. Vesper flew straight, but a gust blew her into a church tower, and Cobble, who had ridden on the roof of the train, was waiting for her on the platform.
qs: Who boasted she could fly faster than the train?
What blew Vesper into a church tower?
How did Cobble get to the next town?

stories.text: Each Saturday Mrs Tembo takes the early boat from her island to the mainland market. She sells woven baskets from a stall under the clock tower until the church bells ring at one. Then she buys rice, lamp oil and a newspaper, and she meets her son, Chilufya, for lunch at a cafe on the quay. The last boat carries her home at five.
qs: Who takes the early boat to the mainland?
Who does she meet for lunch?
When does the last boat carry her home?

stories.text: Captain Ngcobo, who retired from the sea last year, now builds model ships in his garage. His granddaughter, Ayodele, paints the tiny flags, and his dog sleeps under the workbench. This spring one of his models, a three-masted schooner, won first prize at the county show. The judges asked where he had learned to tie such small knots, and he said he had learned on a real ship long ago.
qs: Where does Captain Ngcobo build model ships?
What did Captain Ngcobo retire from?
What won first prize at the county show?

stories.text: A spider called Nettlewick spun her web across the window of a garden shed. A clumsy bumblebee, Barrow, flew into it twice in one morning and tore it both times. The spider was angry at first, but she noticed that the bee always came from the lavender. She moved her web to the other window, and after that the two of them never troubled each other again.
qs: Who spun a web across the window of a garden shed?
How many times did the bee fly into the web?
Where did the spider move her web?

stories.text: On Monday morning a child's red mitten was dropped on the tram. The conductor, Hildegard, found it under a seat and took it to the lost property office at the depot. On Wednesday a woman named Mrs Villaverde came to the depot asking for a mitten, and the clerk gave it back to her. That evening the mitten was back on her daughter's hand at the skating rink.
qs: What was dropped on the tram?
Who came to the depot asking for a mitten?
Where was the mitten that evening?

stories.text: Przemek cut his knee on a rock while he was crabbing with his cousin, Leilani, on Saturday. She helped him limp to the small clinic by the harbour, where Dr Rahimi stitched the cut. The doctor wrapped the knee in a white bandage and told him to keep it dry for a week. Przemek spent Sunday on the sofa, reading comics his cousin had brought from the shop.
qs: What did Przemek cut on a rock?
Who helped Przemek limp to the clinic?
What did the doctor wrap the knee in?

stories.text: Every Saturday, Radoslaw Przybylski, a locksmith, opened his small shop beside the tram stop. One morning a nurse named Uchenna came in because she had locked her keys inside her car. Radoslaw followed her to the hospital car park and opened the door in two minutes. She paid him with a jar of honey from her father's farm.
qs: Who opened a small shop beside the tram stop?
What had Uchenna locked inside her car?
Where did Radoslaw follow her to?
What did she pay him with?

stories.text: A heron named Quilby stood in the shallow river and waited for fish. A young otter swam past and laughed at him for standing still all day. "You splash and chase and catch nothing," said the heron. By evening the otter was hungry, so Quilby showed him how to wait quietly among the reeds.
qs: Who stood in the shallow river?
What was the heron waiting for?
Where did Quilby show the otter how to wait?

stories.text: Lucinda Mensah left her flat in Portwell at seven and drove to the ferry terminal. The ferry carried her across the bay to Skerrin Island, where her grandmother kept goats. They spent the afternoon mending a fence on the hill. Lucinda caught the last ferry home at six, tired but happy.
qs: Who drove to the ferry terminal?
Where did her grandmother keep goats?
What did they mend on the hill?
Where did Lucinda leave from at seven?
When did Lucinda catch the last ferry home?

stories.text: The new librarian, Mr Sadeghi, found a wet umbrella in the children's corner on Monday. Nobody claimed it, so he hung it on a hook by the front desk. On Wednesday a girl called Losana came back for it with her mother. She said she had left it there while she was reading a book about whales.
qs: Where did he find the umbrella?
Who came back for the umbrella?
What did Mr Sadeghi find in the children's corner?

stories.text: Two crows, Ebonet and Sabba, found a shiny ring on a garden wall. Ebonet wanted to keep it in their nest, but Sabba wanted to trade it to the magpie for bread. While they argued, a squirrel ran along the wall and carried the ring away. The crows had neither the ring nor the bread.
qs: Where did the crows find the ring?
What did the crows find on the wall?
What did Sabba want to trade the ring for?

stories.text: At dawn the fishing boat Kestrel left the harbour at Calveston with four men aboard. By noon they had reached the deep water past the lighthouse, and the nets were lowered. The wind rose in the afternoon, so Captain Tullock turned the boat back early. They tied up at the harbour before dark with a hold full of mackerel.
qs: Who turned the boat back early?
When did the boat leave the harbour?
What was the hold full of?

stories.text: Folasade Agbaje, who drives the number nine bus, noticed an old man asleep at the last stop. She woke him gently and asked where he lived. He had missed his stop by six streets because he had been dreaming of the sea. Folasade drove him back on her next trip and waved as he climbed down.
qs: Who drives the number nine bus?
Who was asleep at the last stop?
Where was the old man asleep?
What had he been dreaming of?
How many streets had he missed his stop by?

stories.text: A tortoise named Tumelo carried his house on his back, and a snail laughed because hers was so much smaller. When the rain came, the snail hid under a leaf, but the leaf blew away. Tumelo let her shelter under the edge of his shell until the storm passed. Afterwards the snail never laughed at him again.
qs: Who carried his house on his back?
Where did the snail hide when the rain came?
What did Tumelo carry on his back?

stories.text: On Tuesday morning Haakon and his daughter Runa took the train from Eskmoor to the coast. They ate sandwiches in the dining car and counted windmills from the window. In the afternoon they walked along the cliffs to an old stone chapel. That night they slept at an inn called the Copperkettle.
qs: When did they take the train?
What did they eat in the dining car?
What did they count from the window?
Where did they sleep that night?

stories.text: The baker on Saxby Street, a cheerful woman named Benedetta, ran out of flour on the busiest day of the year. Her neighbour, Mr Marchetti, owned a pizza shop and lent her two sacks. In return she baked him a cake shaped like a pizza. He laughed so hard that he put it in his window for everyone to see.
qs: What did Mr Marchetti lend her?
What did Benedetta bake for him?
Where did he put the cake?

stories.text: A goat named Juniper wanted to reach the apples at the top of the orchard tree. She asked the tall horse to shake the branches, but he was too proud to help a goat. Then a small wren pecked at the stems until three apples dropped. Juniper shared them with the wren, and the horse got none.
qs: Who wanted to reach the apples?
Who was too proud to help?
What did Juniper ask the horse to shake?

stories.text: Early on Friday, a parcel of seeds left a warehouse in Tobermill on the back of a lorry. By lunchtime it had reached the post office in Ravelston Square, where a clerk sorted it. Later a postman named Ozan carried it up the hill on his bicycle. The parcel finally arrived at Mrs Okwuosa's allotment just before the gate was locked.
qs: What left a warehouse in Tobermill?
Where had the parcel reached by lunchtime?
Who carried the parcel up the hill?
What did Ozan ride up the hill?
Whose allotment did the parcel arrive at?

stories.text: When the lift in the tower block broke, the caretaker, Thorvald, carried shopping up the stairs for the older tenants. Mrs Olabisi on the ninth floor gave him tea and a slice of plantain bread. A repair team came on Thursday and fixed the lift by evening. Thorvald said his legs were glad.
qs: Who carried shopping up the stairs?
When did the repair team come?

stories.text: In a dry summer the frogs of Muddle Pond asked the old toad, Grisham, where to find water. Grisham told them about a spring hidden under the ferns behind the barn. The frogs hopped there at night, while the farm cat was asleep. They stayed by the spring until the autumn rain filled their pond again.
qs: Who did the frogs ask about water?
When did the frogs hop to the spring?

stories.text: Zuzana Novakova started her morning at the flower market, where she bought tulips and lilies. At ten she carried them to her stall outside the railway station. Business was slow until the afternoon trains arrived. By five o'clock every bunch was gone, and she took the bus home to Vellmar.
qs: What did Zuzana buy at the flower market?

stories.text: Doctor Mirembe, the only vet in the village, was called to a farm late one night. A cow named Clover was having trouble with her calf. The doctor stayed in the barn until sunrise, and the calf was born healthy. The farmer's children named the calf Dawn because of the time she arrived.
qs: Who was called to a farm late one night?
Why did the children name the calf Dawn?
Where did the doctor stay until sunrise?
Who was having trouble with her calf?

stories.text: A proud peacock named Velasquez spread his feathers every day beside the farm pond. One morning a plain brown hen walked over and asked him to help find her lost chick. The peacock said he was too busy being admired. The hen found the chick herself, hiding under the cart, and after that the other birds stopped admiring the peacock.
qs: Who spread his feathers beside the farm pond?
Who asked the peacock for help?
Why did the peacock not help?

stories.text: Amaru set out from his village before sunrise with three llamas loaded with salt. He crossed the salt flats during the cool morning and rested in the shade of a rock at midday. In the evening he reached the market town of Tamzara. There he traded the salt for cloth, tea and a new pair of sandals.
qs: How many llamas did Amaru take?
Where did he rest at midday?
What were the llamas loaded with?

stories.text: Hiroshi Watanabe repairs shoes in a narrow shop near the bridge. On Monday a schoolteacher brought him boots with a broken heel, and he promised them for Friday. The heel took longer than he expected because the leather was very old. Still, the boots were ready on Thursday afternoon, a day early.
qs: Why did the heel take longer?

stories.text: A mole called Winnow lived under a meadow and could not see the stars. Every night a moth told him what they looked like. One spring the mole dug a tunnel to the top of a hill so that he could feel the night wind. The moth sat on his nose and described each star, and Winnow said it was the best night of his life.
qs: Who told Winnow what the stars looked like?
Where did the mole dig a tunnel to?
What did Winnow want to feel?

stories.text: The school trip left Kirrawee at eight in two yellow buses. First the children visited a chocolate factory, where they watched sweets roll along a belt. After lunch they went to the botanical gardens to draw cactus plants. Their teacher, Miss Calloway, counted them twice before the buses drove home.
qs: What did the children watch roll along a belt?
Where did they go after lunch?

stories.text: Every winter the twins, Eliska and Matej, cleared snow from their grandfather's path. This year he gave them a sled that he had built when he was a boy. It was heavier than the plastic ones their friends had, but it was much faster. The twins raced it down Bexley Hill until their mittens were soaked.
qs: Who cleared snow from the path?
Whose path did the twins clear?
What did their grandfather give them?
Where did the twins race the sled?

stories.text: A beaver named Oakley built a dam that made a quiet pool in the stream. The fish liked the pool, but a family of ducks complained that the water was too still for racing. Oakley opened a small gap in the dam, so the water rushed through one side. Now the fish rest in the pool and the ducks race in the rapids.
qs: What did Oakley open in the dam?

stories.text: In the morning the river barge Bluebell was loaded with timber at the sawmill. It floated slowly downstream past three villages and under a stone bridge. At dusk it reached the city docks, where cranes lifted the timber onto carts. The bargeman, Orvell, slept on board and started back the next day.
qs: What was the barge loaded with?
When did it reach the city docks?
What lifted the timber onto carts?

stories.text: Grace Nakamura opened a small cafe in an old bookshop and kept many of the books on the shelves. Customers could read while they drank their coffee, and some of them bought the books too. A retired sailor, Mr Lindvall, came every morning and read only books about ships. When he finished the last one, Grace ordered more from a dealer in the capital.
qs: Where did Grace open her cafe?

stories.text: Two ants, Tilda and Mabo, found a crumb of cake that was too big for either of them. Tilda pulled from the front while Mabo pushed from behind, but they kept going in different directions. A beetle watched them and told them to walk the same way. With the beetle's advice, they carried the crumb home before the rain.
qs: Who found a crumb of cake?
Who told the ants to walk the same way?
When did the ants carry the crumb home?

stories.text: Inspector Valdivia took the night train from the capital and arrived in Penhallow at dawn. She went straight to the harbour office, where the stolen ledger had last been seen. By noon she had followed a trail of muddy boot prints to a fish warehouse. The ledger was found inside a crate of ice, and the inspector caught the evening train home.
qs: What did the inspector follow to a warehouse?

stories.text: Mrs Brouwer, a retired piano teacher, heard the boy next door practising the same song badly every evening. Instead of complaining, she knocked on his door and offered him free lessons. The boy, Tarquin, learned quickly. At the spring concert in the town hall he played the song perfectly and bowed to her in the front row.
qs: Who was practising the song badly?
Where was Mrs Brouwer sitting at the concert?

stories.text: A hedgehog named Burdock was afraid of the dark and never left his log at night. One evening his friend the owl offered to fly above him and call out whenever danger was near. Together they crossed the whole wood to see a pond full of glowing beetles. After that, Burdock still preferred the day, but he was no longer afraid.
qs: Who was afraid of the dark?
Who offered to fly above Burdock?
What did Burdock never leave at night?
What was the pond full of?

stories.text: At half past six Teodora Popescu locked her shop and walked to the stadium with her brother. They sat high in the north stand and watched the match under bright lights. After the final whistle the crowd poured into the streets, so they waited in a noodle bar until it was quieter. They got home just before midnight.
qs: Who locked her shop at half past six?
Who went to the stadium with Teodora?
What did they watch under bright lights?
Where did they wait after the match?

stories.text: The new postwoman, Habiba, kept getting lost among the farms because none of the gates had numbers. An old farmer named Gwilym painted a number on every gate along the lane. Habiba thanked him with a box of biscuits, and he shared them with his sheepdog. Now she finishes her round an hour earlier.
qs: Who kept getting lost among the farms?
Who painted a number on every gate?
Who did Gwilym share the biscuits with?
How much earlier does Habiba finish her round?

stories.text: Kibo, a young elephant, liked to spray the zebras at the waterhole until they ran off. One hot day the waterhole dried up, and the zebras would not tell Kibo where they had found fresh water. Kibo said sorry to each of them in turn. The oldest zebra then led the whole herd to a hidden river beyond the hills.
qs: Who liked to spray the zebras?
What dried up on the hot day?
What did Kibo say to each zebra?
Where did the oldest zebra lead the herd?

stories.text: Thursday was moving day for the Boateng family. In the morning a van took their beds and boxes from the old flat on Wrexton Road to a house by the canal. The children rode with their aunt, Afua, who stopped for ice cream on the way. By evening the beds were up, and everyone slept in the new house.
qs: Where did the van take the beds from?
Who did the children ride with?

stories.text: A lorry driver named Henrik Tarkowski found a lost puppy at a petrol station. He could not leave it there in the cold, so it rode with him all the way to the coast. At the next depot a mechanic recognised the puppy from a poster. The owner, a girl in a red coat, collected it that evening.
qs: Where did he find the puppy?
What had the mechanic seen the puppy on?

stories.text: A young cockerel named Cobb crowed long before sunrise and woke the whole farm. The pig grumbled, the cows complained, and the farmer threw a boot at the henhouse. The old cockerel, Rufio, taught Cobb to watch the eastern sky for the first grey light. From then on the farm slept until the proper time.
qs: What did Cobb learn to watch?

stories.text: Hyacinth Morrow flew from her home in the mountains to visit her son in a desert city. The plane landed late in the afternoon, and he met her at the airport with a bunch of roses. The next morning they rode camels to a ruined fort. On the third day she flew home with sand still in her shoes.
qs: Who flew to visit her son?
What was still in her shoes?
Where did her son meet her?
Where did they ride camels to?

stories.text: The school cook, Mrs Mehdizadeh, makes soup for two hundred children every day. One Tuesday the gas went off just before lunch. She borrowed three camping stoves from the scout hall next door and still served the soup on time. The head teacher gave her a card that had been signed by every child.
qs: Where did she borrow the stoves from?
How many camping stoves did she borrow?
What did the head teacher give her?

stories.text: A spider called Silka spun her web across the garden gate every night, and every morning the gardener walked through it. At last she asked a bee for advice. The bee told her to build beside the gate instead, between the rose bush and the wall. The gardener never touched that web, and Silka caught more flies than ever.
qs: Who spun her web across the garden gate?
Who walked through the web every morning?
What did Silka ask the bee for?
Where did the bee tell her to build?
What did Silka catch more of?

stories.text: Before school Tavita walked his little sister to the nursery at the end of Kowhai Lane. Then he ran to the bus stop and caught the bus to the high school. After the last lesson he collected his sister and took her to the park, where they fed the ducks. Their mother picked them up from the park gate at five.
qs: Who did Tavita walk to the nursery?
What did they feed at the park?
When did their mother pick them up?

stories.text: Firefighters in the town of Brelland rescued a kitten from a drainpipe on Sunday. The kitten had been stuck for two days before a jogger heard it crying. Officer Mendez used a small camera to find it, and the pipe was cut open carefully. The kitten has been adopted by the jogger, who named it Pipe.
qs: How many days had the kitten been stuck?

stories.text: Every Tuesday, Siv Solheim, a piano tuner, visits the music school on Larch Hill. This week the oldest piano had a broken string, and she had to order a new one from a shop in Brennvik. While she waited, the headmaster, Mr Ekundayo, made her a cup of mint tea. The string arrived on Thursday and she fixed the piano before the spring concert.
qs: Who visits the music school every Tuesday?
What was wrong with the oldest piano?
Who made her a cup of mint tea?

stories.text: A tortoise named Pudrick kept a garden of clover behind a large flat rock. Every night a rabbit crept in and nibbled the best leaves. Pudrick did not shout at him; instead he planted a second row of clover by the fence, which he left for the rabbit. After that the rabbit guarded the garden from the crows, because he finally had food of his own.
qs: Who kept a garden of clover?
What did Pudrick plant by the fence?
What did the rabbit guard the garden from?

stories.text: At seven in the morning, the ferry left Quenby Quay with a cargo of apples. It reached the island of Moskar before nine, where the crew unloaded half the crates. In the afternoon the boat sailed on to Tervik, and the captain, Elodie Brassart, sold the rest of the apples in the market square. The ferry was back at Quenby Quay by sunset.
qs: When did the ferry leave Quenby Quay?
Where did the crew unload half the crates?
Who sold the rest of the apples?
Where was the ferry by sunset?

stories.text: Fatoumata Kone runs a small bakery on Drabble Lane with her brother Sekou. He starts work at four because the bread must be ready when the shop opens. One winter morning the oven would not light, so Fatoumata called an engineer named Radek Ruzicka. He replaced a worn part, and by eight the first loaves were on the shelves.
qs: Who runs the bakery with Fatoumata?

stories.text: Near a dry riverbed lived a lizard called Tasso who liked to boast about his speed. One afternoon a beetle asked him to carry a seed to the top of the dune. Tasso ran so fast that he dropped the seed halfway and never noticed. The beetle walked slowly behind him, picked it up, and planted it himself.
qs: Who liked to boast about his speed?
What did the beetle ask him to carry?
Where was the seed supposed to go?

stories.text: On Saturday morning Rahel and her grandfather took the train from Ostervale to the coast. They spent the morning on the beach at Lunsford, where Rahel found a white shell shaped like a fan. After lunch they walked to the lighthouse, which was painted red and green. They caught the last train home and arrived in Ostervale after dark.
qs: Who took the train with Rahel?
Where did they spend the morning?
What colours was the lighthouse painted?
When did they arrive in Ostervale?

stories.text: Dr Chinwe Obi, the only vet in the village of Gorsedale, was called to a farm late on Sunday night. A cow named Pearl had cut her leg on a wire fence. The farmer, a quiet man called Gunnar, held a lamp while the vet cleaned and stitched the wound. By Wednesday Pearl was walking around the meadow again.
qs: Who was called to a farm late on Sunday night?
What had Pearl cut her leg on?
Where was Pearl walking by Wednesday?

stories.text: Two crows, Kesh and Ombra, found a shiny ring in a puddle. Kesh wanted to hide it in their nest, but Ombra said it belonged to the girl who fed them every morning. They argued until the sun went down. In the end Ombra dropped the ring on the girl's windowsill, and the next day she left them twice as many crumbs.
qs: Where did the crows find a ring?
Who wanted to hide the ring?
Whose ring did Ombra say it was?
Who dropped the ring on the windowsill?
What did the girl leave them the next day?

stories.text: The delivery van left the depot in Carrow at eight. Its first stop was a florist in Lowick, where the driver, Nurlan Demirel, picked up twenty boxes of tulips. He drove them north to a hotel in Askby and had lunch in its kitchen. At three o'clock the empty van was back in Carrow.
qs: When did the van leave the depot?
Where did he pick up the tulips?
How many boxes of tulips did he pick up?
What did the driver pick up?

stories.text: When the roof of the community hall began to leak, the neighbours on Cobbler Row met to decide what to do. Ama Okafor, who worked as a carpenter, offered to fix the beams. Her neighbour Gianluca, a retired teacher, collected money for new tiles from every house on the street. The hall was dry again before the autumn rains.
qs: Who offered to fix the beams?
Who collected money for new tiles?
What did Gianluca collect money for?
What did Ama offer to fix?

stories.text: A young goat named Fescue climbed higher than any goat on the mountain. One day he got stuck on a narrow ledge and could not turn round. An eagle circling above told him to look only at his front feet and step backwards. Fescue did as she said, and he reached the meadow by nightfall.
qs: Who climbed higher than any goat on the mountain?
Who told him what to do?
What did the eagle tell him to look at?
When did he reach the meadow?

stories.text: Early on Monday, Professor Haruki Tanabe flew from Kessington to a conference in Valmont. He gave his talk about glaciers in the main hall at eleven. In the evening he took a bus into the mountains and stayed at a small inn beside a frozen lake. On Tuesday he collected ice samples there before flying home.
qs: Who flew to a conference in Valmont?
What was beside the small inn?
Where did he stay in the mountains?
What did he collect on Tuesday?

stories.text: Ignacy Pomeroy has delivered post in the town of Rellby for thirty years. Every dog on his route knows him, because he carries biscuits in his coat pocket. Last week his bicycle was stolen from outside the library. The children of the town saved their pocket money and bought him a new one.
qs: Who has delivered post in Rellby?
How long has he delivered post?
What does he carry in his coat pocket?
Where was his bicycle stolen from?
Who bought him a new bicycle?

stories.text: A mole named Mudwick was tired of the dark, so he dug a tunnel up to the riverbank. There he met a kingfisher who described the colours of the sky. Mudwick could not see them well with his small eyes, but he liked listening to her. Every evening after that he came up to hear her stories, while she perched on a willow branch.
qs: Who described the colours of the sky?

stories.text: The school trip began at the gates of Fernhall Primary at half past eight. A coach took the class to the science museum in Bradmoor, where they watched a show about volcanoes. At noon they ate sandwiches in the park opposite the museum. Their teacher, Miss Verhoeven, counted them twice before the coach drove back.
qs: When did the school trip begin?
Where did the coach take the class?
What did they eat at noon?

stories.text: Dilara, a nurse at the city hospital, finished her night shift at six in the morning. On the way home she stopped at a cafe run by an old man named Haldor. He noticed she looked tired and gave her a warm roll for free. The next evening she brought him a bunch of yellow roses.
qs: Who is a nurse at the city hospital?
What did she finish at six in the morning?
What did he give her for free?
What did she bring him the next evening?

stories.text: A family of ants was carrying grain across a path when a heavy rain began. The smallest ant, Pepita, found a fallen leaf and pulled it over the grain like a roof. The other ants laughed at first, but their own grain was soon washed away. That night the queen chose Pepita to lead the next journey.
qs: What did Pepita pull over the grain?
What began while the ants were carrying grain?
Who chose Pepita to lead the next journey?

stories.text: In the morning a fisherman named Joao Pereira rowed out from Calheta Cove to check his nets. He found them full of sardines and rowed back to the harbour by ten. His wife, Conceicao, sold the fish at the stall near the church until lunchtime. In the afternoon the whole family carried the nets up to the cliff path to dry in the wind.
qs: Who rowed out to check his nets?
What were the nets full of?
When was he back at the harbour?
Where did the family carry the nets?

stories.text: Anjali Raman started work as the new librarian in Upper Wexham on a rainy Monday. She found hundreds of books still packed in boxes in the cellar. With help from two students, Mathis and Yasmeen, she put them on the shelves over three weekends. The mayor, who had not visited the library for years, came to the reopening.
qs: Who started work as the new librarian?
Where did she find the packed books?
Who helped her put the books on the shelves?
How long did it take to shelve the books?

stories.text: A bear named Ursol woke early from his winter sleep because his stomach was rumbling. He wandered into the valley and found that the bees had not yet made any honey. A squirrel offered him a handful of nuts she had buried in the autumn. Ursol thanked her, and in summer he shared the first honeycomb with her.
qs: Who woke early from his winter sleep?
Why did the bear wake early?
Who offered him a handful of nuts?
What did Ursol share with her in summer?

stories.text: On Friday the Lukusa family moved from a small flat in the city to a farmhouse near Pembry. The removal lorry was loaded by nine and reached the farmhouse at noon. The piano was too wide for the front door, so the men carried it in through the kitchen. By evening the children had chosen their rooms in the attic.
qs: When did the Lukusa family move?
Where did the family move to?
What reached the farmhouse at noon?
What was too wide for the front door?
How did the men get the piano in?

stories.text: Every summer Babatunde Bankole grows tomatoes in the yard behind his barber shop. This year a storm knocked down the canes, and half the plants were broken. His customers, who had eaten his tomatoes for years, came with string and new canes. By August he was handing out baskets of tomatoes to everyone who came in for a haircut.
qs: Who grows tomatoes behind his barber shop?
Who came with string and new canes?
What was he handing out by August?

stories.text: A hedgehog called Quillet wanted to cross the busy road to reach the orchard. She waited at the edge until an old owl told her about a pipe that ran under the road. Quillet crawled through the pipe, which was cold and full of leaves. On the other side she found apples lying in the grass, and she brought one back for the owl.
qs: Who wanted to cross the busy road?
Where did Quillet want to go?
Who told her about the pipe?
How did Quillet get under the road?
What did she find lying in the grass?

stories.text: Captain Morwenna Echeverria flew the morning flight from Rosmere to the island of Tauka. The plane landed at half past ten, and the passengers walked across the runway to a tiny wooden terminal. While the plane was refuelled, Morwenna bought a coconut from a stand by the gate. At one o'clock she flew back to Rosmere with a box of letters for the mainland.
qs: Who flew the morning flight to Tauka?
Where did the morning flight go?
What did she carry back to Rosmere?

stories.text: Aigerim Bolat teaches swimming at the public pool in Darrowfield. On Saturdays she gives free lessons to adults who never learned as children. Her oldest pupil, a seventy-year-old farmer called Ezekiel, swam a full length for the first time last month. Everyone at the pool clapped, and he bought cakes for the whole class.
qs: Who teaches swimming at the public pool?
When does she give free lessons?
Who swam a full length for the first time?
What did Ezekiel buy for the class?

stories.text: A proud peacock named Velvo refused to share the pond with the ducks. He spread his tail and told them his feathers were too fine to get wet. When a fox came through the reeds that evening, the ducks swam to the middle of the pond. Velvo could not swim, so he had to hide in a thorn bush all night and lost three of his feathers.
qs: Who refused to share the pond?
Who did Velvo refuse to share the pond with?
Where did Velvo hide all night?
How many feathers did he lose?

stories.text: Before dawn, two climbers, Maartje and Rafferty, left their tent at the foot of Mount Elvary. They reached a frozen waterfall by eight and stopped to drink tea from a flask. The summit was covered in cloud, so they turned back at the stone hut below the ridge. They were in the village of Selby Cross in time for supper.
qs: Who left their tent before dawn?
What did they reach by eight?
What did they drink from a flask?
Where were they in time for supper?

stories.text: When the old bridge in Kellmouth was closed for repairs, Kayode Ezeh, a boat builder, offered to row his neighbours across the river. Each morning he made six trips before breakfast. A baker on the far bank paid him in bread, and the children who rode with him paid him in drawings. The bridge reopened in May, but Kayode still rows people across on Sundays.
qs: Who rowed his neighbours across the river?
How many trips did he make before breakfast?
What did the children pay him in?

stories.text: A field mouse named Nubbin found a lost kitten crying under a hay cart. Most mice would have run away, but Nubbin led the kitten back to the barn where its mother was searching for it. The mother cat promised never to hunt in Nubbin's corner of the field. From then on the mice there gathered seeds without fear.
qs: Where did Nubbin lead the kitten?
Who promised never to hunt in Nubbin's corner?
What did the mice gather without fear?

stories.text: On Wednesday afternoon a parcel left a warehouse in Grantley on a lorry bound for the coast. It was sorted overnight at a depot in Mirefield, where a machine read its label. On Thursday morning a postwoman named Yaroslava Kovalenko carried it up the hill to the last cottage in Wenlow. Inside the parcel was a pair of red boots for a girl called Leokadia.
qs: When did the parcel leave the warehouse?
Who carried the parcel up the hill?

stories.text: Sunita, the owner of a small shoe shop, noticed that an elderly customer came in every week but never bought anything. One day she asked him why, and he said his own shop had stood in the same place forty years ago. He had been a shoemaker himself, and he liked the smell of leather. Sunita gave him a stool by the window, and now he mends shoes for her on Fridays.
qs: Who owns the small shoe shop?
Who came in every week but never bought anything?
What had the elderly customer been?
Where did Sunita put a stool for him?
When does he mend shoes for her?

stories.text: Once a young whale named Oro swam too close to the shore and was trapped in a shallow bay when the tide went out. A flock of gulls flew back and forth to keep his skin wet with water from the sea. A crab who lived under a rock told Oro to stay calm and save his strength. At midnight the tide came in again, and Oro swam out to his family.
qs: Who was trapped in a shallow bay?
Who told Oro to stay calm?
When did the tide come in again?

stories.text: Every Thursday, Grandma Hallveig takes the number nine bus from her flat in Southbury to the market in Ashwell. She buys fish at the first stall and flowers from a young man named Tesfaye. At eleven she meets her sister for coffee in a cafe beside the clock tower. She is home by one, just in time for the radio quiz.
qs: Who takes the number nine bus?
Where does the bus take her?
When does she meet her sister?
What does she get home in time for?

stories.text: Thiago Albuquerque fixes bicycles in a garage on the corner of Tanner Street. Most of his customers are students from the college, who often cannot pay much. He lets them pay with small jobs, like sweeping the floor or painting the sign. Last spring one student, Michiko, painted a bright blue bicycle on the garage door, and now everyone in town knows where to find him.
qs: Who fixes bicycles on Tanner Street?
Who are most of his customers?
What do the students pay with?

stories.text: A spider called Wisp spun her web between two sunflowers in a farmer's garden. Each morning the dew made the web shine, and a vain dragonfly came to admire himself in the drops. One day he flew too close and got caught. Wisp let him go on the promise that he would warn her whenever the farmer came with his shears.
qs: Who spun her web between two sunflowers?
What did the farmer come with?
Who came to admire himself in the drops?
Why did the dragonfly get caught?

stories.text: Late on Sunday night, the circus trucks rolled into a field outside Pellworth. By Monday noon the big tent was up, and the horse trainer, Arvind Pillai, was leading the horses to the river to drink. The first show began at seven that evening. On Saturday the trucks were packed again and the circus moved on to Dorrington.
qs: Where did the circus trucks arrive on Sunday night?
What was up by Monday noon?
Who led the horses to the river?
When did the first show begin?
Where did the circus move on to?

stories.text: Kavitha Krishnan and her husband Omar run a soup stall at the bus station in Kirkton. In winter the drivers queue for her lentil soup before their early shifts. Omar bakes the flatbread at home the night before, while Kavitha chops the vegetables. On the coldest day of the year they gave soup away to anyone waiting for the late bus.
qs: Who runs the soup stall with Kavitha?
Who queues for her lentil soup?

stories.text: In a beech wood lived an old badger called Ruthven who could no longer dig. Every autumn the younger badgers laughed at his empty den. One cold winter, though, a storm flooded their deep tunnels, and only the shallow den of Ruthven on the hill stayed dry. He let them all sleep there until spring, and they never laughed at him again.
qs: Who laughed at his empty den?
Where was the den of Ruthven?
How long did the younger badgers sleep there?

stories.text: At six in the morning, Lyudmila Krol, an engineer, drove from her house in Vellmore to a wind farm on the coast. She climbed the tallest turbine to replace a broken sensor and finished before the wind grew strong. At two she stopped at a roadside diner for soup. She was back in Vellmore before the school bus dropped her son at the gate.
qs: Who drove to a wind farm?
Where did she stop at two?

stories.text: Every evening, Rohini and her younger brother Kabir walk a grey greyhound called Nimbus, because its owner, Mr Takeda, has a bad knee. They take Nimbus along the canal and back past the bakery. One evening Nimbus ran after a cat and pulled Kabir into a puddle. Mr Takeda laughed so hard when he saw them that he forgot about his knee.
qs: Who walks the dog with Rohini?
Why can Mr Takeda not walk the dog?
